sentences.zh: 李敏，字公勉，襄城人。

translations.literal: Li Min, styled Gongmian, was a native of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Min, whose style was Gongmian, came from Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 天順初，奉敕撫定貴州蠻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun, by imperial order he pacified the Miao of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign he received an imperial commission to pacify the tribal peoples of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 還，巡按畿內。

translations.literal: On his return he toured and inspected the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he was assigned to inspect the metropolitan districts.

sentences.zh: 以薊州餉道經海口，多覆溺，建議別開三河達薊州，以避其險，軍民利之。

translations.literal: Because the Ji supply route passed through Haikou and many boats capsized, he proposed opening another route by three rivers to reach Ji Prefecture and avoid the danger; soldiers and civilians alike benefited.
translations.idiomatic: The grain route to Ji Prefecture ran through Haikou, where many boats were lost; he proposed a new channel along three rivers to reach Ji and avoid the hazard, to the great benefit of troops and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 成化初，用薦超遷浙江按察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, on recommendation he was promoted beyond the usual pace to investigating commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chenghua reign he was recommended and promoted ahead of schedule to investigating commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 再任湖廣。

translations.literal: He served a second term in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He held a second appointment in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 歷山西、四川左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of left and right provincial administration commissioner of Shanxi and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then served in turn as left and right provincial administration commissioner in Shanxi and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十三年擢右副都御史，巡撫大同。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and appointed grand coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was raised to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and appointed grand coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 敵騎出沒塞下，掩殺守墩軍，敏伏壯士突擒之。

translations.literal: Enemy horsemen appeared below the passes and ambushed the garrison troops on the watchtowers; Min hid bold warriors and charged out to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy cavalry raided along the border and slaughtered the troops manning the watchtowers, Min concealed picked warriors and rushed out to capture them.

sentences.zh: 修治垣塹，敵不敢犯。

translations.literal: He repaired the walls and ditches, and the enemy did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the walls and moats, and the enemy no longer dared to strike.

sentences.zh: 十五年召為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was summoned as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was recalled to serve as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 逾四年，病歸。

translations.literal: After more than four years he fell ill and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: More than four years later he fell ill and went home.

sentences.zh: 河南大饑，條上救荒數事。

translations.literal: When Henan suffered a great famine, he submitted a memorial listing several measures for famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan was stricken by severe famine, he memorialized with several proposals for relief.

sentences.zh: 詔以左副都御史巡撫保定諸府。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Vice Censor-in-chief of the Left to grand coordinate the prefectures of Baoding and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as Vice Censor-in-chief of the Left and grand coordinator of Baoding and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二十一年改督漕運，尋召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year his assignment was changed to supervising grain transport; soon afterward he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was reassigned to supervise the grain-transport system, and soon after was summoned to the post of Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 先是，敏在大同，見山東、河南轉餉至者，道遠耗費，乃會計歲支外，悉令輸銀。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Min was in Datong, he had seen grain shipped from Shandong and Henan arrive after great distance and expense; he then calculated the annual expenditure and ordered that beyond fixed needs all be paid in silver.
translations.idiomatic: While still at Datong, Min had observed how costly it was to haul grain from Shandong and Henan over long distances; he reckoned the annual outlay and directed that all surplus deliveries be rendered in silver instead.

sentences.zh: 民輕賫易達，而將士得以其贏治軍裝，交便之。

translations.literal: The people found silver lighter and easier to deliver, while officers and soldiers could use the surplus to equip the army—both parties found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Silver was easier for the people to carry and deliver, while officers and soldiers could apply the savings to military equipment; both sides found the arrangement advantageous.

sentences.zh: 至是，並請畿輔、山西、陜西州縣歲輸糧各邊者，每糧一石征銀一兩，以十九輸邊，依時值折軍餉，有余則召糴以備軍興。

translations.literal: Now he also requested that for the counties and prefectures of the capital region, Shanxi, and Shaanxi that each year sent grain to the various border posts, for every picul of grain one tael of silver be levied: nineteen parts for the border, with military rations converted at timely rates; any remainder to purchase grain for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: He now proposed that for every county and prefecture in the capital region, Shanxi, and Shaanxi that annually forwarded grain to the border, one tael of silver be collected per picul of grain—nineteen parts for border supply, with military pay converted at current rates, and any surplus used to buy grain against wartime need.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 自是北方二稅皆折銀，由敏始也。

translations.literal: From this time the two taxes of the north were all converted to silver—all begun by Min.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the two grain levies of the north were commuted to silver—a reform that began with Min.

sentences.zh: 崇文門宣課司稅，多為勢要所侵漁。

translations.literal: Taxes at the Chongwen Gate Revenue Office were largely siphoned off by powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue collected at the Chongwen Gate tax office was largely diverted by powerful interests.

sentences.zh: 敏因馬文升言請增設御史主事監視。

translations.literal: At Ma Wensheng's suggestion Min requested additional censors and clerks to supervise collection.
translations.idiomatic: Following Ma Wensheng's advice, Min asked that additional censors and clerks be appointed to oversee collection.

sentences.zh: 御史陳瑤斥敏聚斂，敏再疏求去。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Yao denounced Min for amassing wealth; Min memorialized again asking to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Yao accused Min of extortion; Min submitted another memorial requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him and kept him on.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassured him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 貴戚請隙地及鷹房、牧馬場千頃，敏執不可，事得寢。

translations.literal: Noble relatives requested vacant land and a thousand qing of hawk parks and horse pastures; Min held firm and would not yield, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kinsmen sought vacant plots and a thousand qing of hawking grounds and horse pastures; Min refused to yield, and the request was shelved.

sentences.zh: 當憲宗末，中官、佞幸多賜莊田。

translations.literal: Toward the end of Emperor Xianzong's reign, eunuchs and favorites received many estates.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xianzong reign, eunuchs and court favorites were granted large numbers of estates.

sentences.zh: 既得罪，率辭而歸之官，罪重者奪之。

translations.literal: Once they fell from favor they would usually relinquish them to the state; the more severely punished had their land confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When they fell from grace they generally surrendered the land to the government; the more seriously punished had their estates seized outright.

sentences.zh: 然不以賦民。

translations.literal: Yet the land was not taxed from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the fields were not assessed as ordinary tax land on the populace.

sentences.zh: 敏請召佃，畝科銀三分，帝從之，然他莊田如故也。

translations.literal: Min requested that tenants be summoned to cultivate it, with three fen of silver per mu; the emperor agreed, but other estates remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Min proposed summoning tenant farmers and levying three fen of silver per mu; the emperor agreed, but other estates were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 會京師大水，敏乃極陳其害，言：「今畿輔皇莊五，為地萬二千八百余頃；

translations.literal: When the capital suffered great flooding, Min then set forth the harm at length, saying: "At present in the capital region there are five imperial estates, comprising more than twelve thousand eight hundred qing of land;
translations.idiomatic: When severe floods struck the capital, Min laid out the damage in full, writing: "At present there are five imperial estates in the metropolitan region, covering more than 12,800 qing;

sentences.zh: 勛戚、中官莊三百三十有二，為地三萬三千一百余頃。

translations.literal: estates of meritorious kinsmen and eunuchs number three hundred thirty-two, comprising more than thirty-three thousand one hundred qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: and estates held by meritorious kinsmen and eunuchs number 332, covering more than 33,100 qing.

sentences.zh: 官校招無賴為莊頭，豪奪畜產，戕殺人，汙婦女，民心痛傷。

translations.literal: Official runners recruit ruffians as estate managers, who seize livestock by force, kill people, and violate women—the people's hearts are wounded in pain.
translations.idiomatic: Government runners recruit ruffians as estate agents who seize livestock by force, kill people, and assault women, to the anguish of the common people.

sentences.zh: 災異所由生。

translations.literal: This is whence portents and anomalies arise.
translations.idiomatic: Such abuses are what give rise to portents and calamities.

sentences.zh: 皇莊始正統間，諸王未封，相閑地立莊。

translations.literal: Imperial estates began in the Zhengtong period, when the princes had not yet been enfeoffed and idle land was set aside as estates.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial estates began in the Zhengtong era, when the princes had not yet taken up their fiefs and vacant land was set aside as crown holdings.

sentences.zh: 王之藩，地仍歸官，其後乃沿襲。

translations.literal: When a prince went to his fief the land still reverted to the state; only later was the practice continued.
translations.idiomatic: When a prince departed for his fief the land was supposed to revert to the government; only later did the practice persist.

sentences.zh: 普天之下，莫非王土，何必皇莊。

translations.literal: All under heaven is the king's land—why must there be imperial estates?
translations.idiomatic: All land under heaven belongs to the throne—why maintain separate imperial estates?

sentences.zh: 請盡革莊戶，賦民耕。

translations.literal: I request that estate households be entirely abolished and the land taxed and farmed by the people.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that estate stewards be abolished entirely and the fields assessed and farmed by ordinary taxpayers.

sentences.zh: 畝概征銀三分，充各宮用度。

translations.literal: Collect three fen of silver per mu in general, to supply the expenses of the various palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Levy three fen of silver per mu in general to meet the expenses of the palaces.

sentences.zh: 無皇莊之名，而有足用之效。

translations.literal: Without the name of imperial estates, yet with the effect of sufficient supply.
translations.idiomatic: There would be no name of imperial estates, yet the same adequate revenue.

sentences.zh: 至權要莊田，亦請擇佃戶領之，有司收其課，聽諸家領取。

translations.literal: As for the estates of powerful figures, I also request that tenant households be chosen to manage them, with the local authorities collecting the dues and the various families receiving their shares.
translations.idiomatic: As for estates of the powerful, I also ask that tenant farmers be selected to work them, with local officials collecting the rent and the owners receiving their due.

sentences.zh: 悅民心，感和氣，無切於此。」

translations.literal: To please the people's hearts and harmonize the vital energies—nothing is more urgent than this."
translations.idiomatic: To win the people's hearts and restore harmony—nothing is more urgent."

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time it could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 南京御史與守備太監蔣琮相訐，御史鹹逮謫，而琮居職如故。

translations.literal: A Nanjing censor exchanged accusations with the garrison eunuch Jiang Cong; all the censors were arrested and demoted while Jiang kept his post as before.
translations.idiomatic: When a Nanjing censor clashed with the garrison eunuch Jiang Cong, every censor involved was arrested and banished while Jiang remained in office.

sentences.zh: 敏再疏力爭，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Min memorialized twice, arguing forcefully, but in neither case was he heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Min memorialized twice in protest, but both times his pleas went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，得疾乞休，帝為遣醫視療。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he fell ill and asked to retire; the emperor sent physicians to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he fell ill and requested retirement; the emperor sent physicians to attend him.

sentences.zh: 已，復力請，乃以葉淇代，詔敏乘傳歸。

translations.literal: Afterward he again pressed his request, and Ye Qi was appointed in his stead; an edict ordered Min to return home by relay post.
translations.idiomatic: When he pressed again, Ye Qi was appointed in his place and Min was ordered home by imperial relay.

sentences.zh: 未抵家卒。

translations.literal: Before he reached home he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before reaching home.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚恭靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Gongjing.

sentences.zh: 敏生平篤行誼，所得祿賜悉以分昆弟、故人。

translations.literal: Throughout his life Min was devoted to righteous conduct; whatever salary and gifts he received he divided among brothers and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Min lived by steadfast loyalty and friendship, sharing every salary and gift among his brothers and old companions.

sentences.zh: 裏居時，築室紫雲山麓，聚書數千卷，與學者講習。

translations.literal: While living at home he built a lodge at the foot of Purple Cloud Mountain, gathered several thousand volumes, and lectured with scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he built a study at the foot of Purple Cloud Mountain, collected several thousand books, and lectured with local scholars.

sentences.zh: 及巡撫大同，疏籍之於官，詔賜名紫雲書院。

translations.literal: While grand coordinating Datong he memorialized to register it with the government; an edict granted the name Purple Cloud Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When he later served as grand coordinator of Datong, he memorialized to register the academy with the government, and an edict bestowed the name Purple Cloud Academy.

sentences.zh: 大同孔廟無雅樂，以敏奏得頒給如制雲。

translations.literal: The Confucian temple at Datong had no court music; through Min's memorial it was issued according to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Confucian temple at Datong lacked court music until Min's memorial secured its provision according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 葉淇，字本清，山陽人。

translations.literal: Ye Qi, styled Benqing, was a native of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Qi, whose style was Benqing, came from Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 天順初，石亨譖之下吏，考訊無驗，出為武陟知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun, Shi Heng slandered him and had him sent to the judicial authorities; examination found no evidence, and he was released to serve as magistrate of Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianshun, Shi Heng framed him and had him imprisoned; interrogation found no proof, and he was released to serve as magistrate of Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 成化中累官大同巡撫。

translations.literal: During Chenghua he rose through offices to grand coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign he rose through successive posts to grand coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，召為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, he was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Qi was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年代李敏為尚書，尋加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he replaced Li Min as minister, and soon afterward was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he succeeded Li Min as minister and was soon made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 哈密為土魯番所陷，守臣請給其遺民廩食，處之內地，淇曰：「是自貽禍也。」

translations.literal: Hami had fallen to Turfan; the garrison officials requested grain rations for the surviving people and resettlement in the interior. Qi said: "This would be inviting disaster upon ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: When Hami fell to Turfan, local officials asked to feed the refugees and resettle them inland. Qi said, "That would be inviting disaster upon ourselves."

sentences.zh: 寢其奏。

translations.literal: The memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 奸民獻大名地為皇莊，淇議歸之有司。

translations.literal: Wicked commoners offered land in Daming as an imperial estate; Qi proposed returning it to the local authorities.
translations.idiomatic: When scheming locals offered Daming land as an imperial estate, Qi argued that it be returned to civil administration.

sentences.zh: 內官龍綬請開銀礦，淇不可。

translations.literal: The eunuch Long Shou requested opening silver mines; Qi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Long Shou petitioned to open silver mines; Qi refused.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with him.

sentences.zh: 已，綬請長蘆鹽二萬引，鬻於兩淮以供織造費。

translations.literal: Afterward Shou requested twenty thousand salt certificates from Changlu to sell in the two Huai circuits to supply weaving expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Later Long Shou asked for 20,000 Changlu salt certificates to sell in the two Huai regions to fund the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 淇力爭，竟不納。

translations.literal: Qi argued forcefully, and in the end it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: Qi fought the proposal vigorously, and it was ultimately rejected.

sentences.zh: 淇居戶部六年，直亮有執，能為國家惜財用。

translations.literal: Qi held the Ministry of Revenue for six years, upright and principled, able to husband the state's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Qi headed the Ministry of Revenue for six years, upright and firm in principle, and skilled at guarding the state's finances.

sentences.zh: 每廷議用兵，輒持不可。

translations.literal: Whenever the court debated military action, he invariably held that it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court debated war, he invariably opposed it.

sentences.zh: 惟變開中之制，令淮商以銀代粟，鹽課驟增至百萬，悉輸之運司，邊儲由此蕭然矣。

translations.literal: Only in changing the Kaizhong system, ordering Huai merchants to pay silver instead of grain, did salt revenue suddenly rise to a million, all paid to the transport offices—border stores were thereby depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he altered the Kaizhong salt-exchange system so that Huai merchants paid in silver rather than grain; salt revenue suddenly leapt to a million taels, all diverted to the transport offices, and border granaries were left bare.

sentences.zh: 九年四月乞休，歸卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year he asked to retire; he died after returning home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year he requested retirement and died after returning home.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 從子贄，進士，歷官刑部右侍郎，以清操聞。

translations.literal: His nephew Zan, a jinshi, rose to Vice Minister of Justice and was known for pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zan, a jinshi, rose to Vice Minister of Justice and was renowned for integrity.

sentences.zh: 賈俊，字廷傑，束鹿人。

translations.literal: Jia Jun, styled Tingjie, was a native of Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Jun, whose style was Tingjie, came from Shulu.

sentences.zh: 以鄉舉入國學。

translations.literal: By provincial examination he entered the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the provincial examination, he entered the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 天順中，選授御史。

translations.literal: During Tianshun he was selected and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshun reign he was selected and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 歷巡浙江、山西、陜西、河南、南畿，所至有聲。

translations.literal: He successively inspected Zhejiang, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Henan, and the southern capital region; wherever he went he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: He served successive inspection tours in Zhejiang, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Henan, and the southern metropolitan region, earning a reputation wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 成化十三年，自山東副使超拜右僉都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Chenghua, from vice commissioner of Shandong he was promoted beyond the usual pace to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and appointed grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Chenghua he was promoted ahead of schedule from vice commissioner of Shandong to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 在鎮七年，軍民樂業，召為工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was at his post seven years; soldiers and civilians lived in contentment, and he was summoned as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in the post, with troops and civilians prospering, he was recalled as Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十一年奉敕振饑河南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, by imperial order he relieved famine in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he received an imperial commission to relieve famine in Henan.

sentences.zh: 尋轉左，數月拜尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the left post, and within months was appointed minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the left vice ministership and within months was appointed minister.

sentences.zh: 時專重進士，舉人無至六卿者，俊獨以重望得之。

translations.literal: At the time only jinshi were heavily favored; no holder of the provincial degree had risen to one of the Six Ministers—Jia Jun alone attained it through his great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The court then favored jinshi exclusively, and no provincial graduate had ever reached one of the Six Ministries; Jun alone attained that rank on the strength of his reputation.

sentences.zh: 及孝宗踐阼，尚書王恕、李敏、周洪謨、余子俊、何喬新，都御史馬文升，皆一時民譽，俊參其間，亦稱職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, the ministers Wang Su, Li Min, Zhou Hongmo, Yu Zijun, He Qiaoxin, and Censor-in-chief Ma Wensheng were all men of the people's praise at the time; Jun among them also performed his duties well.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, the ministers Wang Su, Li Min, Zhou Hongmo, Yu Zijun, and He Qiaoxin, together with Censor-in-chief Ma Wensheng, were the most admired statesmen of the day; Jun served among them and also acquitted himself well.

sentences.zh: 諸王府第、塋墓悉官予直，而儀仗時繕修。

translations.literal: The mansions and tombs of all princely establishments were wholly paid for at official rates, while ceremonial regalia was repaired from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Princely mansions and tombs were all paid for at official rates, and ceremonial regalia was repaired on a regular schedule.

sentences.zh: 內官監欲頻興大工，俊言王府既有祿米、莊田，請給半直；

translations.literal: The Directorate of Palace Eunuchs wished frequently to launch major works. Jun said that since princely establishments already had salary grain and estate lands, only half payment should be granted;
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch directorate wanted to launch major projects repeatedly. Jun argued that since princes already received salary grain and estate income, only half payment should be granted;

sentences.zh: 儀仗非甚敝，不得煩有司；

translations.literal: if ceremonial regalia was not badly worn, the civil authorities should not be troubled;
translations.idiomatic: and unless ceremonial regalia was badly worn, civil officials should not be burdened;

sentences.zh: 公家所宜營，惟倉庫、城池，余皆停罷。

translations.literal: what the state ought to undertake were only storehouses and city walls—all else should be halted.
translations.idiomatic: the state should build only storehouses and city walls, and suspend everything else.

sentences.zh: 帝報可。

translations.literal: The emperor replied that it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，中官奏修沙河橋，請發京軍二萬五千及長陵五衛軍助役。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, eunuchs memorialized to repair the Shahe Bridge and requested dispatching twenty-five thousand capital troops and the five guards of Changling to assist.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, eunuchs petitioned to repair the Shahe Bridge and asked for 25,000 capital troops plus the five Changling guards to assist.

sentences.zh: 內府寶鈔司乞增工匠。

translations.literal: The Imperial Treasury Bureau of the inner palace requested additional artisans.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace treasury bureau sought additional artisans.

sentences.zh: 浙江及蘇、松諸府方罹水災而織造錦綺至數萬匹。

translations.literal: Zhejiang and the prefectures of Suzhou and Songjiang had just suffered floods while orders for brocade and silk reached tens of thousands of bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang and the Suzhou–Songjiang region had just been hit by floods even as orders for tens of thousands of bolts of brocade and silk arrived.

sentences.zh: 俊皆執奏，並得寢。

translations.literal: Jun in every case memorialized firmly, and all were shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Jun held firm on each petition, and every request was shelved.

sentences.zh: 工部政務與內府監局相表裏，而內官監專董工役，職尤相關。

translations.literal: The affairs of the Ministry of Works were intertwined with the inner palace directorates, and the Directorate of Eunuchs especially oversaw labor service—the offices were closely linked.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Works business was intertwined with inner palace directorates, and the eunuch directorate in particular controlled labor levies, so the offices were tightly linked.

sentences.zh: 俊不為所撓，工役大省。

translations.literal: Jun was not swayed by them, and labor service was greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Jun refused to be swayed, and corvée labor was sharply reduced.

sentences.zh: 太廟後殿成，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 足疾，致仕。

translations.literal: He had foot ailment and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Afflicted with a foot ailment, he retired.

sentences.zh: 詔許乘傳歸，給夫廩如制。

translations.literal: An edict permitted him to return home by relay post and granted porters and grain rations according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed him to return by imperial relay with porters and grain rations as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died a little over a year later.

sentences.zh: 俊廉慎，居工部八年，望孚朝野。

translations.literal: Jun was incorrupt and cautious; he held the Ministry of Works eight years, and trust in him filled court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was incorrupt and cautious. During eight years at the Ministry of Works he enjoyed the trust of court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 代之者劉璋，字廷信，延平人。

translations.literal: His successor Liu Zhang, styled Tingxin, was a native of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: His successor Liu Zhang, whose style was Tingxin, came from Yanping.

sentences.zh: 天順初進士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination early in the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官中外有聲。

translations.literal: He held offices inside and outside the capital with renown.
translations.idiomatic: He served at court and in the provinces with a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 居工部，亦數有爭執，名亞於俊。

translations.literal: While at the Ministry of Works he also had several disputes; his fame was slightly below Jun's.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Works he too had several clashes with the court, though his standing remained slightly below Jun's.

sentences.zh: 黃紱，字用章，其先封丘人。

translations.literal: Huang Fu, styled Yongzhang, was originally from Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fu, whose style was Yongzhang, was originally from Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖徙平越，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather moved to Pingyue, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather moved to Pingyue, where the family then settled.

sentences.zh: 紱登正統十三年進士，除行人，歷南京刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Fu passed the jinshi in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong, was appointed courier, and served as director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Fu passed the jinshi in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong, became a courier, and rose to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 剛廉，人目之曰「硬黃」。

translations.literal: Upright and incorrupt, people called him "Hard Huang."
translations.idiomatic: Fiercely upright, people nicknamed him "Hard Huang."

sentences.zh: 大猾譚千戶者，占民蘆場，莫敢問，紱奪還之民。

translations.literal: A great scoundrel, Commander Tan, seized commoners' reed grounds and none dared challenge him; Fu took them back for the people.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful rogue, Commander Tan, had seized commoners' reed lands with impunity until Fu restored them to their owners.

sentences.zh: 成化九年，遷四川左參議。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chenghua he was transferred to Left Assistant Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Chenghua he was transferred to Left Assistant Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 久之，進左參政。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Left Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was promoted to Left Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 按部崇慶，旋風起輿前，不得行。

translations.literal: While inspecting Chongqing, a whirlwind rose before his sedan and he could not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: While on inspection in Chongqing, a whirlwind rose before his sedan chair and blocked his way.

sentences.zh: 紱曰：「此必有冤，吾當為理。」

translations.literal: Fu said: "There must be a grievance here; I shall investigate it."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "There must be a grievance here, and I shall see justice done."

sentences.zh: 風遂散。

translations.literal: The wind then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The wind then died away.

sentences.zh: 至州，禱城隍神，夢若有言州西寺者。

translations.literal: Arriving at the prefecture, he prayed to the city-god, and in a dream seemed to be told of a temple west of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the prefectural seat he prayed to the city god and dreamed of something concerning a temple west of the city.

sentences.zh: 寺去州四十里，倚山為巢，後臨巨塘。

translations.literal: The temple was forty li from the prefecture, built against the mountain with a great pond behind.
translations.idiomatic: The temple stood forty li from the city, built against a mountain with a great pond behind it.

sentences.zh: 僧夜殺人沈之塘下，分其資。

translations.literal: The monks killed people by night and sank them in the pond, dividing their goods.
translations.idiomatic: By night the monks murdered travelers and sank the bodies in the pond, dividing the loot.

sentences.zh: 且多藏婦女於窟中。

translations.literal: They also hid many women in caves.
translations.idiomatic: They also kept many women hidden in caves.

sentences.zh: 紱發吏兵圍之，窮詰，得其狀，誅僧毀其寺。

translations.literal: Fu sent officials and soldiers to surround them, questioned them to the end, obtained the facts, executed the monks, and destroyed the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Fu sent officials and troops to surround the place, examined the case fully, obtained proof, executed the monks, and destroyed the temple.

sentences.zh: 倉吏倚皇親乾沒官糧巨萬，紱追論如法，威行部中。

translations.literal: A granary clerk, relying on imperial kin, embezzled tens of thousands of piculs of government grain; Fu pursued prosecution according to law, and his authority prevailed throughout the province.
translations.idiomatic: A granary clerk, shielded by imperial kin, embezzled tens of thousands of piculs of state grain; Fu prosecuted him by law, and his authority ran throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 歷四川、湖廣左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of left and right provincial administration commissioner of Sichuan and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as left and right provincial administration commissioner in Sichuan and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 奏閉建昌銀礦。

translations.literal: He memorialized to close the Jianchang silver mines.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to shut the Jianchang silver mines.

sentences.zh: 兩京工興，湖廣當輸銀二萬，例征之民，紱以庫羨充之。

translations.literal: When construction was launched in both capitals, Huguang was to supply twenty thousand taels of silver, customarily levied on the people; Fu used surplus in the treasury to meet it.
translations.idiomatic: When both capitals launched construction, Huguang owed 20,000 taels of silver, normally levied on the people; Fu covered it from treasury surplus.

sentences.zh: 荊王奏徙先壟，紱恐為民擾，執不可。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jing memorialized to move his ancestors' tombs; Fu feared trouble for the people and held firm that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jing asked to relocate his ancestral tombs; Fu, fearing harm to the people, refused.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢右副都御史，巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and appointed grand coordinator of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and appointed grand coordinator of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 劾參將郭鏞，都指揮鄭印、李鐸、王琮等抵罪，計捕奸豪張綱。

translations.literal: He impeached Assistant Commander Guo Yong and the regional commanders Zheng Yin, Li Duo, Wang Cong, and others, who were punished; he also planned the capture of the outlaw Zhang Gang.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Assistant Commander Guo Yong and regional commanders Zheng Yin, Li Duo, Wang Cong, and others, who were punished, and organized the capture of the outlaw Zhang Gang.

sentences.zh: 申軍令，增置墩堡，邊政一新。

translations.literal: He enforced military discipline, added watchtowers and forts, and border administration was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened military discipline, added watchtowers and forts, and renewed border administration.

sentences.zh: 出見士卒妻衣不蔽體，嘆曰：「健兒家貧至是，何面目臨其上。」

translations.literal: Going out he saw soldiers' wives in clothing that did not cover their bodies and sighed: "The strong warriors' families are so poor—what face have I to stand above them?"
translations.idiomatic: On inspection he saw soldiers' wives in rags and sighed, "Our fighting men' families are this destitute—how can I face them as their commander?"

sentences.zh: 亟豫給三月餉，親為拊循。

translations.literal: He immediately advanced three months' pay and personally comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately advanced three months' pay and went among them to offer comfort.

sentences.zh: 會有詔毀庵寺，紱因盡汰諸尼，以給壯士無妻者。

translations.literal: When an edict came to destroy nunneries, Fu took the opportunity to dismiss all nuns and assign them to unmarried soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered nunneries destroyed, Fu dismissed the nuns and assigned them to unmarried soldiers.

sentences.zh: 及紱去，多攜子女拜送於道。

translations.literal: When Fu departed, many brought their children to bow to him along the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu left, many brought their children to bow to him along the road.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年，拜南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi he was appointed Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongzhi he was appointed Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 言官以紱進頗驟，頻有言。

translations.literal: Censors said Fu's advancement had been rather rapid, and there was frequent criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Censors complained that Fu had risen too quickly, and criticism was frequent.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，就改左都御史，焚差歷簿於庭曰：「事貴得人耳，資勞久近，豈立官意哉。」

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen and instead transferred him to Left Censor-in-chief; he burned the seniority roster in the courtyard, saying: "What matters in office is getting the right man—how can length of service be the basis for appointment?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them and made him Left Censor-in-chief; he burned the seniority roster in the courtyard, saying, "Offices depend on the right men—seniority alone should not govern appointment."

sentences.zh: 紱歷官四十余年，性卞急，不能容物。

translations.literal: Fu had held office more than forty years; his nature was brusque and impatient and he could not tolerate others.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had served more than forty years. Blunt and impatient by nature, he could not easily tolerate others.

sentences.zh: 然操履潔白，所至有建樹。

translations.literal: Yet his conduct was pure and white; wherever he went he achieved results.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his conduct was spotless, and wherever he served he left solid achievements.

sentences.zh: 六年乞休，未行卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he asked to retire; before he could depart he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he asked to retire but died before leaving office.

sentences.zh: 張悅，字時敏，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, styled Shimin, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue, whose style was Shimin, came from Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 舉天順四年進士，授刑部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun he passed the jinshi and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Justice, rising to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the fourth year of Tianshun, entered the Ministry of Justice as a clerk, and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 成化中出為江西僉事，改督浙江學校。

translations.literal: During Chenghua he went out as Jiangxi Vice Commissioner and was transferred to supervise schools in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua he served as Jiangxi Vice Commissioner, then was transferred to supervise schools in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 力拒請托，校士不糊名，曰：「我取自信而已。」

translations.literal: He firmly rejected solicitations; in examining scholars he did not seal names, saying: "I rely on my own judgment alone."
translations.idiomatic: He firmly rejected patronage, and in examining candidates he refused sealed names, saying, "I trust my own judgment."

sentences.zh: 遷四川副使，進按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Sichuan Vice Commissioner and promoted to investigating commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Sichuan Vice Commissioner and promoted to investigating commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遭喪，服闋補湖廣。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning; when mourning ended he was reassigned to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his parent he was reassigned to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 王府承奉張通縱恣，悅繩以法。

translations.literal: The princely establishment attendant Zhang Tong was insolent; Yue restrained him by law.
translations.idiomatic: The princely attendant Zhang Tong acted lawlessly; Yue held him to the law.

sentences.zh: 及入覲，中官尚銘督東廠，眾競趨其門，悅獨不往。

translations.literal: When he entered the capital for audience, the eunuch Shang Ming supervised the Eastern Depot and everyone rushed to his door; Yue alone did not go.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the capital, the eunuch Shang Ming supervised the Eastern Depot and everyone flocked to his gate; Yue alone stayed away.

sentences.zh: 銘銜甚，伺察無所得。

translations.literal: Ming bore a deep grudge and watched for faults but found none.
translations.idiomatic: Ming resented him deeply and spied on him but found nothing.

sentences.zh: 銘敗，召拜左僉都御史。

translations.literal: When Ming fell, Yue was summoned as Left Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming fell from power, Yue was summoned as Left Vice Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，遷工部右侍郎，轉吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, he was moved to Vice Minister of Works, then to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Yue was moved to Vice Minister of Works and then to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 王恕為尚書，悅左右之，嘗兩攝選事。

translations.literal: Wang Su was minister, and Yue assisted him; he twice handled selection affairs in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was minister of personnel, and Yue assisted him, twice handling appointments in his place.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年夏，大旱，求言。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year of Hongzhi there was great drought, and the court sought advice.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year of Hongzhi a great drought struck, and the court sought counsel.

sentences.zh: 陳遵舊章、恤小民、崇儉素、裁冗食、禁濫罰數事。

translations.literal: He set forth restoring old regulations, cherishing the common people, honoring frugality, cutting redundant consumption, and forbidding excessive punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He urged restoring old regulations, caring for commoners, promoting frugality, cutting redundant spending, and forbidding excessive punishments.

sentences.zh: 又上修德、圖治二疏。

translations.literal: He also submitted two memorials on cultivating virtue and governing the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted two memorials on cultivating virtue and governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 並嘉納。

translations.literal: All were praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: All were praised and accepted.

sentences.zh: 俄遷南京右都御史，就改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Right Censor-in-chief at Nanjing, then transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Right Censor-in-chief at Nanjing, then made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年復改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was again transferred to the Ministry of War to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred again to the Ministry of War to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 以年至，累疏乞休。

translations.literal: Because of age he memorialized repeatedly asking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: On grounds of age he repeatedly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子少保，馳傳歸。

translations.literal: An edict made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and ordered him home by relay post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and sent him home by imperial relay.

sentences.zh: 卒贈太子太保，謚莊簡。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Zhuangjian.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Zhuangjian.

sentences.zh: 時與悅同里而先為南京兵部尚書者張鎣，字廷器，正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Jin of the same native place, who earlier had been Minister of War at Nanjing, styled Tingqi, passed the jinshi in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Jin of the same county, who had earlier been Minister of War at Nanjing, styled Tingqi, had passed the jinshi in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，擢御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai he was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign he was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 歷江西副使按察使、陜西左布政使。

translations.literal: He successively served as Jiangxi Vice Commissioner, investigating commissioner, and Shaanxi Left Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Jiangxi Vice Commissioner, investigating commissioner, and Shaanxi Left Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 成化三年以右副都御史巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chenghua he was made Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chenghua he was made Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 寧夏城，土築，鎣始甃以磚。

translations.literal: The city of Ningxia was of rammed earth; Jin was the first to face it with brick.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia city was earthen; Jin was the first to face its walls with brick.

sentences.zh: 道河流，溉靈州屯田七百余頃。

translations.literal: He channeled river water and irrigated more than seven hundred qing of garrison fields at Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He channeled river water and irrigated more than seven hundred qing of garrison farmland at Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以父喪去。

translations.literal: He left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服除，起撫河間諸府，改大同，歷刑部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed to grand coordinate the prefectures of Hejian, then transferred to Datong, and served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he grand coordinated Hejian and neighboring prefectures, then Datong, and served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十八年擢本部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to minister of that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 明年加太子少保。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 又明年，再以憂歸。

translations.literal: The year after that he again returned home on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he again retired for mourning.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年起南京兵部尚書，卒官，贈太子太保，謚莊懿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi he was recalled as Minister of War at Nanjing, died in office, and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Zhuangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongzhi he was recalled as Minister of War at Nanjing, died in office, and was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Zhuangyi.

sentences.zh: 似鐘，字大器，鄆城人。

translations.literal: Si Zhong, styled Daqi, was a native of Yuncheng.
translations.idiomatic: Si Zhong, whose style was Daqi, came from Yuncheng.

sentences.zh: 成化二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授御史，巡鹽兩淮。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor and inspected salt in the two Huai circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor and inspected salt administration in the two Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 按浙江還，掌諸道章奏。

translations.literal: After inspecting Zhejiang he returned to handle memorials from all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After inspecting Zhejiang he returned to handle memorials from all circuits.

sentences.zh: 汪直諷鐘劾馬文升，鐘不可，被譖杖闕下。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi prompted Zhong to impeach Ma Wensheng; Zhong refused and was slandered and beaten at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi urged Zhong to impeach Ma Wensheng; Zhong refused, was framed, and was beaten at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 以都御史王越薦，擢大理寺丞，再遷右少卿。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Censor-in-chief Wang Yue he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then again to Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On Censor-in-chief Wang Yue's recommendation he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then to Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 寇入大同，廷議遣大臣巡視保定諸府，乃以命鐘。

translations.literal: When bandits entered Datong, the court debated sending a senior minister to inspect the prefectures of Baoding and the like, and the task was given to Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders entered Datong, the court debated sending a senior minister to inspect Baoding and neighboring prefectures, and Zhong was chosen.

sentences.zh: 居數月，即擢右副都御史巡撫其地。

translations.literal: Within several months he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of the region.

sentences.zh: 河間瀕海民地為勢家所據，鐘奪還之。

translations.literal: Coastal lands of Hejian near the sea had been seized by powerful families; Zhong took them back.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal farmland in Hejian had been seized by powerful families; Zhong restored it to the people.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，僦運艘載母柩南還。

translations.literal: During mourning for his mother he hired transport boats to carry her coffin south.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother he hired transport boats to carry her coffin south.

sentences.zh: 督漕總兵官王信奏之，逮下吏。

translations.literal: The commander supervising grain transport, Wang Xin, memorialized against him, and he was arrested and sent to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-transport commander Wang Xin reported him, and he was arrested and sent to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 會當路方逐尹旻黨，而鐘與旻為同鄉，乃貶二秩為曲靖知府，改徽州，復入為大理寺左少卿。

translations.literal: At the time those in power were driving out the faction of Yin Min, and since Zhong was a fellow townsman of Min's he was demoted two ranks to prefect of Qujing, transferred to Huizhou, then recalled as Left Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power were then purging Yin Min's faction; because Zhong was Min's fellow townsman he was demoted two ranks to prefect of Qujing, transferred to Huizhou, then recalled as Left Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年，以右副都御史巡撫蘇、松諸府，盡心荒政。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi he was made Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of the prefectures of Suzhou and Songjiang, devoting himself wholeheartedly to famine administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongzhi he was made Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Suzhou and Songjiang, devoting himself entirely to famine relief.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部侍郎總督倉場，尋改吏部。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue to supervise the granaries, and soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue to supervise the granaries, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一年遷右都御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was moved to Right Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became Right Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 居二年，進戶部尚書。

translations.literal: After two years he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十五年，上天下會計之數，言：「常入之賦，以蠲免漸減，常出之費，以請乞漸增，入不足當出。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor ordered accounts for the realm, and Zhong said: "Regular revenue is gradually reduced through exemptions, while regular expenditure gradually increases through petitions—receipts no longer meet disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the emperor ordered a national accounting, and Zhong wrote: "Regular revenue keeps shrinking through tax relief, while regular spending keeps growing through special requests—income no longer covers outgo.

sentences.zh: 正統以前軍國費省，小民輸正賦而已。

translations.literal: Before Zhengtong, military and state expenses were few, and the common people paid only the standard tax.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhengtong, military and state expenses were modest and commoners paid only the standard levy.

sentences.zh: 自景泰至今，用度日廣，額外科率。

translations.literal: From Jingtai to the present, expenditures grow daily and extra levies multiply.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jingtai reign to now, spending has widened daily and surcharges have multiplied.

sentences.zh: 河南、山東邊餉，浙江、雲南、廣東雜辦，皆昔所無。

translations.literal: Border rations for Henan and Shandong, and miscellaneous levies for Zhejiang, Yunnan, and Guangdong, were all unknown in earlier times.
translations.idiomatic: Border rations in Henan and Shandong and miscellaneous levies in Zhejiang, Yunnan, and Guangdong were all unknown in earlier times.

sentences.zh: 民已重困，無可復增。

translations.literal: The people are already heavily burdened and cannot bear further increase.
translations.idiomatic: The people are already crushed and cannot bear more.

sentences.zh: 往時四方豐登，邊境無調發，州縣無流移。

translations.literal: In former times the four quarters were abundant, the borders had no emergency levies, and prefectures and counties had no displaced persons.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the realm was abundant, the borders needed no emergency levies, and prefectures and counties saw no displaced people.

sentences.zh: 今太倉無儲，內府殫絀，而冗食冗費日加於前。

translations.literal: Now the Great Granary has no stores, the inner treasury is exhausted, while redundant consumption and redundant spending increase daily.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Great Granary is empty, the inner treasury exhausted, while redundant mouths and redundant spending grow by the day.

sentences.zh: 願陛下惕然省憂，力加損節。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will be vigilant in anxiety and strive to cut and economize.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to be alert to this danger and strive to cut waste.

sentences.zh: 且敕廷臣共求所以足用之術。」

translations.literal: Moreover command the court ministers together to seek means to make revenue sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: And command the court ministers together to find ways to make revenue sufficient."

sentences.zh: 帝乃下廷臣議。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered court ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered court ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 議上十二事，其罷傳奉冗官，汰內府濫收軍匠，清騰驤四衛勇士，停寺觀齋醮，省內侍、畫工、番僧供應，禁王府及織造濫乞鹽引，令有司征莊田租，皆權幸所不便者。

translations.literal: Their deliberation set forth twelve measures: abolishing redundant officials on special appointment, cutting excessive intake of artisans and soldiers in the inner palace, clearing the four guards of Tengxiang, stopping temple sacrifices and fasting, reducing supplies to inner attendants, painters, and Tibetan monks, forbidding princely establishments and weaving offices from begging salt certificates at will, and ordering local officials to collect estate rents—all measures inconvenient to powerful favorites.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed twelve measures: abolishing redundant special appointees, cutting excessive intake of artisans and soldiers in the inner palace, clearing the four Tengxiang guards, stopping temple sacrifices, reducing supplies to inner attendants, painters, and Tibetan monks, forbidding princes and weaving offices from begging salt certificates at will, and ordering local officials to collect estate rents—each unwelcome to powerful favorites.

sentences.zh: 疏留數月不下，鐘乃復言之。

translations.literal: The memorial was held several months without action; Zhong memorialized again.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial sat for months without action, and Zhong raised it again.

sentences.zh: 他皆報可，而事關權幸者終格不行。

translations.literal: Other items were approved, but those touching powerful favorites were ultimately blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Other items were approved, but those touching powerful favorites were blocked.

sentences.zh: 奸商投外戚張鶴齡，乞以長蘆舊引十七萬免追鹽課，每引納銀五分，別用價買各場余鹽如其數，聽鬻販，帝許之。

translations.literal: Wicked merchants attached themselves to the maternal kin Zhang Heqing and begged that one hundred seventy thousand old Changlu certificates be exempted from salt tax, paying five fen of silver per certificate and separately buying surplus salt from each depot in equal amount to sell freely; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants attached themselves to the empress kin Zhang Heqing and asked that 170,000 old Changlu salt certificates be exempted from tax, paying five fen per certificate while buying surplus salt in equal volume to sell freely; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 後奸民援例乞兩淮舊引至百六十萬，鐘等力持，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Afterward wicked men cited the precedent and begged old certificates in the two Huai circuits up to one million six hundred thousand; Zhong and others argued forcefully, but none were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Later others cited the precedent and sought up to 1.6 million old certificates in the two Huai regions; Zhong and others fought it, but in vain.

sentences.zh: 自此鹽法大壞，奸人橫行江湖，官司無如何矣。

translations.literal: From this the salt laws were greatly corrupted; wicked men ran rampant on the rivers and lakes, and the authorities could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: From this the salt laws collapsed; racketeers dominated the waterways, and officials were powerless.

sentences.zh: 東廠偵事者發鐘子瑞受金事，鐘屢疏乞休，命馳驛歸。

translations.literal: Eastern Depot investigators exposed Zhong son Rui for taking bribes; Zhong memorialized repeatedly asking to retire and was ordered home by relay post.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Depot investigators exposed Zhong son Rui for taking bribes; Zhong repeatedly asked to retire and was sent home by imperial relay.

sentences.zh: 正德時，劉瑾摭鐘在部時事，至罰米者三。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign Liu Jin dredged up matters from Zhong ministry days, and he was fined grain three times.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, Liu Jin dredged up Zhong ministry record and fined him grain three times.

sentences.zh: 又數年卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years later.

sentences.zh: 曾鑒，字克明，其先桂陽人，以戍籍居京師。

translations.literal: Ceng Jian, styled Keming, was originally from Guiyang; his family settled in the capital through military registration.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng Jian, whose style was Keming, was originally from Guiyang; his family settled in the capital through military registration.

sentences.zh: 天順八年進士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianshun he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 通州民十余人坐為盜，獄已具，鑒辨其誣。

translations.literal: More than ten commoners of Tongzhou were convicted as bandits and the case was closed; Jian showed they had been falsely accused.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten Tongzhou commoners were convicted as bandits with the case closed; Jian showed they had been framed.

sentences.zh: 已，果獲真盜。

translations.literal: Afterward the real bandits were indeed captured.
translations.idiomatic: The real bandits were soon captured.

sentences.zh: 成化末，歷右通政，累遷工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Chenghua he served as Right Vice Commissioner of the Court of Transmission and rose to Left Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Chenghua he was Right Vice Commissioner of the Court of Transmission and rose to Left Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年進尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Hongzhi he was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Hongzhi he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 孝宗在位久，海內樂業，內府供奉漸廣，司設監請改造龍毯、素毯一百有奇。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong had reigned long; within the seas the people were content, but inner palace supplies gradually expanded. The Directorate of Palace Eunuchs requested remaking more than one hundred dragon and plain carpets.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong had reigned long; the realm was at peace, but inner palace supplies grew. The eunuch directorate asked to remake more than one hundred dragon and plain carpets.

sentences.zh: 鑒等言：「毯雖一物，然征毛毳於山、陜，采綿紗諸料於河南，召工匠於蘇、松，經累歲，勞費百端。

translations.literal: Jian and others said: "Though a carpet is but one object, wool is levied from Shanxi and Shaanxi, cotton and yarn from Henan, and artisans summoned from Suzhou and Songjiang—over many years the labor and expense are manifold.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and others wrote: "A carpet is a single object, yet wool must be levied from Shanxi and Shaanxi, cotton and yarn from Henan, and artisans summoned from Suzhou and Songjiang—over years the labor and cost are immense.

sentences.zh: 祈賜停止。」

translations.literal: We pray that it be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that this be stopped."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: They were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: They were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 內府針工局乞收幼匠千人，鑒等言：「往年尚衣監收匠千人，而兵仗局效之，收至二千人。

translations.literal: The inner palace Needlework Bureau begged to recruit a thousand young artisans; Jian and others said: "In former years the Imperial Apparel Directorate recruited a thousand artisans, and the Armaments Bureau followed suit, recruiting two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The inner Needlework Bureau asked to recruit a thousand young artisans; Jian and others said: "Years ago the Imperial Apparel Directorate took a thousand artisans, and the Armaments Bureau followed with two thousand.

sentences.zh: 軍器局、司設監又效之，各收千人。

translations.literal: The Military Equipment Bureau and the Directorate of Ceremonial again followed, each recruiting a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Equipment Bureau and Ceremonial Directorate followed again, each taking a thousand.

sentences.zh: 弊源一開，其流無已。」

translations.literal: Once the source of abuse is opened, the flow has no end."
translations.idiomatic: Once such abuse begins, it never ends."

sentences.zh: 於是命減其半。

translations.literal: Thereupon an order halved the number.
translations.idiomatic: The order was then halved.

sentences.zh: 太監李興請辦元夕煙火，有詔裁省，因鑒奏盡罷之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Li Xing requested fireworks for the Lantern Festival; there was an edict to cut and economize, and on Jian memorial they were wholly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Li Xing requested Lantern Festival fireworks; an edict called for cuts, and on Jian memorial they were abolished entirely.

sentences.zh: 十六年，帝納諸大臣言召還織造中官，中官鄧容以請，帝又許之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the emperor accepted senior ministers advice to recall weaving eunuchs; eunuch Deng Rong petitioned again and the emperor again permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the emperor accepted ministers advice to recall weaving eunuchs; eunuch Deng Rong petitioned again and the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 鑒等極言，乃命減三之一。

translations.literal: Jian and others argued forcefully, and an order cut it by one third.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and others protested vigorously, and the order was cut by one third.

sentences.zh: 其冬，言諸省方用兵，且水旱多盜賊，乞罷諸營繕及明年煙火、龍虎山上清宮工作。

translations.literal: That winter he said the provinces were at war and afflicted by flood, drought, and bandits, and begged to halt camp repairs and next year fireworks and work on the Shangqing Palace on Dragon-Tiger Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he noted war, flood, drought, and banditry in the provinces and asked to halt camp repairs, next year fireworks, and work on the Shangqing Palace on Dragon-Tiger Mountain.

sentences.zh: 帝皆報從。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all.

sentences.zh: 孝宗末，閣部大臣皆極一時選，鑒亦持正。

translations.literal: Toward the end of Xiaozong reign the grand secretaries and ministers were all men of the finest selection of the age; Jian also held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Xiaozong reign the grand secretaries and ministers were the finest of the age; Jian too held firm.

sentences.zh: 及與韓文等請誅宦官不勝，諸大臣留者率巽順避禍，鑒獨守故操。

translations.literal: When with Han Wen and others he failed to secure execution of the eunuchs, most senior ministers who remained became compliant and avoided trouble; Jian alone kept his former conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When he and Han Wen failed to secure execution of the eunuchs, most remaining ministers grew compliant; Jian alone kept his old ways.

sentences.zh: 有詔賜皇親夏儒第，帝嫌其隘，欲拓之。

translations.literal: An edict granted a residence to the imperial kin Xia Ru; the emperor found it narrow and wished to expand it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted a mansion to imperial kin Xia Ru; the emperor found it too small and wished to expand it.

sentences.zh: 鑒力爭，不從。

translations.literal: Jian argued forcefully and was not obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian protested vigorously but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 明年春，中官黃準守備鳳陽，從其請，賜旗牌。

translations.literal: The next spring the eunuch Huang Zhun, garrisoning Fengyang, obtained his request and was granted banners and tablets.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring eunuch Huang Zhun, garrisoning Fengyang, obtained banners and tablets at his request.

sentences.zh: 鑒等言大將出征及諸邊守將，乃有旗牌，內地守備無故事，乃寢。

translations.literal: Jian and others said that great generals on campaign and border garrison commanders alone received banners and tablets; for interior garrisons there was no precedent, and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and others said only campaigning generals and border commanders received banners and tablets; interior garrisons had no precedent, and the grant was shelved.

sentences.zh: 其年閏正月致仕。

translations.literal: That intercalary first month he retired.
translations.idiomatic: That intercalary first month he retired.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 梁璟，字廷美，崞縣人。

translations.literal: Liang Jing, styled Tingmei, was a native of Guo County.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Jing, whose style was Tingmei, came from Guo County.

sentences.zh: 天順八年進士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianshun he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 成化時，屢遷都給事中。

translations.literal: During Chenghua he was repeatedly promoted to chief supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua he rose to chief supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 項忠征荊、襄，驅流民復業。

translations.literal: Xiang Zhong campaigned in Jing and Xiang and drove displaced people back to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Zhong campaigned in Jing and Xiang and drove displaced people back to their fields.

sentences.zh: 璟劾其縱兵逼迫，較賊更慘，語具《忠傳》。

translations.literal: Jing impeached him for letting troops drive them by force, more cruel than bandits—the account is in the Biography of Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing impeached him for using troops to drive them by force, more cruel than bandits—as told in Zhong biography.

sentences.zh: 延綏用兵，令山西預征芻粟，民相率逃亡。

translations.literal: When Yan-sui was at war, Shanxi was ordered to levy fodder and grain in advance; the people fled in groups.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan-sui was at war, Shanxi was ordered to levy fodder and grain in advance, and people fled in crowds.

sentences.zh: 璟疏陳其困，得寬減。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized their distress and obtained relief and reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Jing memorialized their distress and won relief.

sentences.zh: 畿輔八府舊止設巡撫一人，駐薊州以禦邊，不能兼顧。

translations.literal: The eight prefectures of the capital region formerly had only one grand coordinator, stationed at Jizhou to guard the border and unable to attend to all.
translations.idiomatic: The eight capital prefectures had only one grand coordinator at Jizhou for border defense and could not cover all.

sentences.zh: 璟請順天、永平二府分設一巡撫，以薊州邊務屬之，令巡撫陳濂專撫保定六府兼督紫荊諸關。

translations.literal: Jing requested a separate coordinator for Shuntian and Yongping, with Jizhou border affairs assigned to him, and Grand Coordinator Chen Lian to specialize in Baoding six prefectures while supervising the Zijing and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: Jing asked for a separate coordinator for Shuntian and Yongping, border affairs at Jizhou under him, and Chen Lian to handle Baoding six prefectures and the Zijing passes.

sentences.zh: 朝議從之，遂為定制。

translations.literal: Court deliberation followed him, and it became permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed, and it became permanent practice.

sentences.zh: 已，與同官韓文、王詔等奏請起致仕尚書王竑、李秉，而斥都御史王越，並及宮闈隱事，被撻文華殿。

translations.literal: Afterward, with fellow officials Han Wen and Wang Zhao and others, he memorialized to recall retired ministers Wang Hong and Li Bing while denouncing Censor-in-chief Wang Yue, also touching on hidden palace matters; they were beaten at the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Han Wen and Wang Zhao, he asked to recall Wang Hong and Li Bing, denounced Wang Yue, and touched on palace secrets; they were beaten in the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 武靖伯趙輔西征不敢戰，稱病求還，復謀典營府事。

translations.literal: Military Marquis Zhao Fu on the western campaign dared not fight, claimed illness and asked to return, yet still schemed to command the capital garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Military Marquis Zhao Fu on the western campaign would not fight, claimed illness to return, yet still sought command of the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 璟等極論其罪，乃令養疾歸。

translations.literal: Jing and others argued his crimes at length, and he was ordered to nurse his illness at home.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and others laid out his crimes, and he was sent home to convalesce.

sentences.zh: 九載秩滿，擢陜西左參政，分守洮、岷。

translations.literal: When his term expired in the ninth year he was promoted to Shaanxi Left Assistant Commissioner, in charge of Tao and Min.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired in the ninth year he became Shaanxi Left Assistant Commissioner, guarding Tao and Min.

sentences.zh: 西番入寇，督兵斬其魁。

translations.literal: Western tribes raided; he directed troops and beheaded their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Western tribes raided; he led troops and beheaded their leader.

sentences.zh: 內艱服闋，還原任，歷左、右布政使。

translations.literal: During mourning for his mother, when mourning ended he returned to his post and served as left and right administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he returned and served as left and right administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先後在陜十五年，多政績。

translations.literal: He was in Shaanxi fifteen years in all, with many achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He spent fifteen years in Shaanxi with many achievements.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，遷右副都御史，巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong succeeded, he was moved to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong succeeded, he became Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，民饑，請免征兩京漕糧八十九萬余石，從之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi the people suffered famine; he requested exemption of eight hundred ninety thousand odd piculs of grain transport to the two capitals, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongzhi famine struck; he secured exemption of more than 890,000 piculs of grain transport to the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 帝登極詔書已罷四方額外貢獻，而提督武當山中官復貢黃精、梅筍、茶芽諸物。

translations.literal: The accession edict had already abolished extra tribute from the four quarters, yet the eunuch supervising Wudang Mountain again presented yellow essence, bamboo shoots, tea buds, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The accession edict had abolished extra tribute, yet the Wudang eunuch again presented yellow essence, bamboo shoots, and tea.

sentences.zh: 武當道士先止四百，至是倍之，所度道童更倍，鹹衣食於官。

translations.literal: Wudang Taoists had formerly been limited to four hundred; now they doubled, and ordained Taoist youths doubled again, all eating at government expense.
translations.idiomatic: Wudang Taoists had been capped at four hundred; now they doubled, ordained youths doubled again, all fed by the state.

sentences.zh: 月給油蠟、香楮，灑掃夫役以千計。

translations.literal: Monthly oil, wax, incense, paper, and more than a thousand sweepers were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly oil, wax, incense, paper, and more than a thousand sweepers were supplied.

sentences.zh: 中官陳喜又攜道士三十余人，各領護持敕，所至張威虐。

translations.literal: Eunuch Chen Xi also brought more than thirty Taoists, each bearing an imperial protective tally, and wherever they went they abused their authority.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Chen Xi also brought thirty-odd Taoists with imperial tallies and abused authority wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 璟皆奏請停免，多見采納。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized to stop or reduce all these; many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Jing memorialized to stop or reduce these abuses; many requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 外艱服除，再撫四川。

translations.literal: After mourning for his father he again grand coordinated Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he again grand coordinated Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 七年召拜南京吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 久之，就進戶部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 致仕歸，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 王詔，字文振，趙人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhao, styled Wenzhen, was a man of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhao, whose style was Wenzhen, was from Zhao.

sentences.zh: 生有異姿，學士曹鼐奇之，妻以女。

translations.literal: At birth he had an unusual appearance; Academician Cao Tai marveled at him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He had an unusual appearance at birth; Academician Cao Tai admired him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 天順末，登進士，授工科給事中。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianshun he passed the jinshi and was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianshun he passed the jinshi and became supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 睿皇后崩，值秋享太廟，時議謂不當以卑廢尊。

translations.literal: When Empress Rui died, it fell on the autumn offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; opinion held that the inferior should not displace the superior.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Rui died during the autumn temple offering, opinion held that mourning should not displace the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 詔言《禮》有喪不祭，無已，則移日俟釋服。

translations.literal: Zhao memorialized that the Rites say when in mourning one does not sacrifice; if unavoidable, the day should be moved to await the end of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao cited the Rites: in mourning one does not sacrifice; if unavoidable, the day should be moved until mourning ends.

sentences.zh: 議雖不行，識者是焉。

translations.literal: Though the proposal was not adopted, those who understood approved.
translations.idiomatic: Though rejected, knowledgeable men approved.

sentences.zh: 勘牧馬草場，劾會昌侯孫繼宗、撫寧侯朱永侵占罪。

translations.literal: Inspecting horse pastures, he impeached Marquis Sun Jizong of Huichang and Marquis Zhu Yong of Funing for encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting horse pastures, he impeached Marquis Sun Jizong of Huichang and Marquis Zhu Yong of Funing for encroachment.

sentences.zh: 時方面官缺，令京卿三品保舉。

translations.literal: At the time regional posts were vacant and third-rank capital officials were ordered to recommend candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Regional posts were vacant and third-rank capital officials were told to recommend candidates.

sentences.zh: 詔言恐長奔競風，不聽。

translations.literal: Zhao said this would encourage frantic competition and was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao warned this would encourage frantic competition; the emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 累遷都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 八年七月敕修隆善寺工竣，授工匠三十人官尚寶少卿，任道遜等以書碑皆進秩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year, when repair of Longshan Temple was completed by imperial order, thirty artisans were made Vice Directors of the Imperial Treasures; Ren Daoxun and others who carved steles were all promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, eighth month, when Longshan Temple repairs finished, thirty artisans were made Vice Directors of the Imperial Treasures and stele carvers were promoted.

sentences.zh: 詔上疏力諫，不省。

translations.literal: Zhao memorialized forcefully in protest but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao protested forcefully but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 已，偕梁璟等論及宮闈事，帝大怒，召至文華殿面詰之，詔仰呼曰：「臣等言雖不當，然區區犬馬之誠，知為國而已。」
