translations.literal: Afterward, with Liang Jing and others, he discussed palace matters; the emperor was greatly angered and summoned them to the Wenhua Hall to question them face to face. Zhao looked up and cried: "Though our words were improper, our humble loyalty as dogs and horses knows only to serve the state."
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Liang Jing, he discussed palace matters; the emperor was furious and questioned them in the Wenhua Hall. Zhao cried out: "Our words may have been wrong, but our loyalty knows only the state."

sentences.zh: 乃杖而釋之。

translations.literal: They were beaten and released.
translations.idiomatic: They were beaten and released.

sentences.zh: 出為湖廣右參政。

translations.literal: He went out as Right Assistant Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Right Assistant Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 原傑經略荊、襄，詔襄理功為多。

translations.literal: Yuan Jie directed affairs in Jing and Xiang; Zhao assisted in the work with great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jie directed affairs in Jing and Xiang; Zhao assisted with great merit.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去。

translations.literal: He left on his father death.
translations.idiomatic: He left to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服除再任，遷右布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he served again and was promoted to Right Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned and was promoted to Right Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，轉貴州左布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi he was transferred to Left Administration Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongzhi he became Left Administration Commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 其冬，以右副都御史巡撫雲南。

translations.literal: That winter he was made Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he became Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 土官好爭襲，所司入其賄，變亂曲直，生邊患。

translations.literal: Native officials loved to fight over succession; local offices took their bribes, twisted right and wrong, and bred border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Native officials fought constantly over succession; local offices took bribes, distorted justice, and bred border trouble.

sentences.zh: 詔不通苞苴，一斷以法，且去弊政之不便者。

translations.literal: Zhao would accept no gifts, judged everything by law, and abolished inconvenient abusive policies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao refused gifts, judged solely by law, and abolished abusive policies that harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 諸夷歸命，邊僥寧戢。

translations.literal: The tribes submitted, and the border was briefly tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes submitted and the frontier grew calm.

sentences.zh: 有故官不能歸者，妻子多鬻為奴。

translations.literal: Former officials who could not return home often had wives and children sold as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Former officials unable to return home often saw wives and children sold into slavery.

sentences.zh: 詔為資遣，得歸者甚眾。

translations.literal: Zhao provided travel funds; very many were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao provided travel funds, and a great many were able to return.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，尚書吳雲繼王祎死事，後祎謚忠文，歲祀之，而不及雲。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu reign Minister Wu Yun followed Wang Yi in dying for the state; later Yi was posthumously titled Zhongwen and sacrificed to yearly, but Yun was not included.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu, Minister Wu Yun had followed Wang Yi to his death for the state; Yi later received the posthumous title Zhongwen and annual sacrifice, but Yun was omitted.

sentences.zh: 詔以為請，乃謚雲忠節，與祎並祀。

translations.literal: Zhao memorialized on his behalf; only then was Yun posthumously titled Zhongjie and sacrificed together with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao memorialized on his behalf, and Yun was posthumously titled Zhongjie and honored alongside Yi.

sentences.zh: 四年召拜南京兵部右侍郎，未上，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing but died before assuming the post.

sentences.zh: 徐恪，字公肅，常熟人。

translations.literal: Xu Ke, styled Gongsu, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ke, whose style was Gongsu, came from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 成化二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 中官欲出領抽分廠，恪等疏爭。

translations.literal: Eunuchs wished to go out and head the tax-collection depots; Ke and others memorialized in protest.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs wanted to head tax-collection depots in person; Ke and others protested by memorial.

sentences.zh: 中官怒，請即遣恪等，將摭其罪，無所得乃已。

translations.literal: The eunuchs were angry and asked that Ke and others be sent out immediately so they could gather crimes against them; finding nothing, they desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs were furious and demanded Ke be sent out at once so they could find crimes against him; finding none, they relented.

sentences.zh: 出為湖廣左參議，遷河南右參政。

translations.literal: He went out as Left Assistant Commissioner of Huguang and was transferred to Right Assistant Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left Assistant Commissioner of Huguang, then Right Assistant Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 陜西饑，當轉粟數萬石。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered famine and was to transfer tens of thousands of piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi was in famine and owed tens of thousands of piculs in grain transfers.

sentences.zh: 恪以道遠請輸直，上下稱便。

translations.literal: Ke, because the route was long, requested payment in cash instead; above and below all praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Ke asked to pay cash instead because of the long route, and the change pleased everyone.

sentences.zh: 恪素剛正。

translations.literal: Ke was by nature upright and firm.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was upright and unyielding by nature.

sentences.zh: 所至，抑豪右，祛奸弊。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he suppressed powerful families and removed corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he curbed powerful families and removed corruption.

sentences.zh: 及為巡撫，以所部多王府，持法尤嚴，宗人多不悅。

translations.literal: As grand coordinator his jurisdiction held many princely establishments; he held the law especially strict, and many of the clan were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: As grand coordinator he governed many princely establishments, enforced the law strictly, and displeased many of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 平樂、義寧二王遂訐恪減祿米、改校尉諸事。

translations.literal: The Princes of Pingle and Yining then accused Ke of reducing salary grain and changing bodyguards and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Pingle and Yining accused him of cutting salary grain and altering bodyguards.

sentences.zh: 勘無驗，坐恪入王府誤行端禮門，欲以平二王忿。

translations.literal: Investigation found no proof; Ke was punished for entering a princely mansion by mistake through the Duanli Gate, intending to appease the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation found no proof; Ke was punished for mistakenly entering a princely mansion through the Duanli Gate to appease the two young princes.

sentences.zh: 帝知恪無他，而以二王幼，降敕切責，命湖廣巡撫韓文與恪易任。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Ke had no other fault but, because the princes were young, sent a stern edict of rebuke and ordered Huguang Grand Coordinator Han Wen to exchange posts with Ke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Ke was otherwise blameless but, because the princes were young, rebuked him sternly and swapped him with Han Wen.

sentences.zh: 吏民罷市，泣送數十里不絕。

translations.literal: Officials and people closed the markets and wept, seeing him off for more than ten li without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners closed the markets and wept, escorting him for miles without end.

sentences.zh: 屬吏以羨金贐，揮之去。

translations.literal: Subordinates offered surplus funds as a parting gift; he waved them away.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates offered surplus funds as a farewell gift; he refused.

sentences.zh: 至則值岐王之國，中使攜鹽數百艘，抑賣於民，為恪所持阻不行。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi went to his fief, eunuchs brought hundreds of salt boats and forced sales on the people; Ke held them back and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qi departed for his fief, eunuchs brought hundreds of salt boats and forced sales on the people; Ke blocked them.

sentences.zh: 其黨密構於帝。

translations.literal: Their faction secretly framed him before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Their faction secretly denounced him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 居一歲，中旨改南京工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: After one year an imperial order from the inner palace transferred him to Right Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After a year an inner-palace order moved him to Right Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 恪上疏曰：「大臣進用，宜出廷推，未聞有傳奉得者。

translations.literal: Ke memorialized: "Promotion of great ministers should come from court recommendation; I have never heard of appointment by special relay.
translations.idiomatic: Ke wrote: "Senior ministers should be promoted by court recommendation; I have never heard of appointment by special relay.

sentences.zh: 臣生平不敢由他途進，請賜罷黜。」

translations.literal: Throughout my life I have never dared advance by another path; I beg to be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: I have never sought advancement by any other path; I beg dismissal."

sentences.zh: 帝慰留，乃拜命。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him and he accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassured him and he accepted.

sentences.zh: 勢要家濫索工匠者，悉執不予。

translations.literal: Powerful families who begged artisans indiscriminately—he seized none of them for them.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families who demanded artisans arbitrarily received none from him.

sentences.zh: 十一年考績入都，得疾，遂致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he entered the capital for merit review, fell ill, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he came to the capital for merit review, fell ill, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 李介，字守貞，高密人。

translations.literal: Li Jie, styled Shouzhen, was a native of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jie, whose style was Shouzhen, came from Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 成化五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，改御史，巡鹽兩浙，還掌河南道事。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin academician, changed to investigating censor, inspected salt in the two Huai circuits, and on return handled affairs of the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin, became investigating censor, inspected salt in the two Huai regions, and on return handled the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 以四方災傷，陳時政數事，帝多采用之。

translations.literal: Because the four quarters suffered disaster and injury, he set forth several items on current policy, many of which the emperor adopted.
translations.idiomatic: With disasters across the realm, he memorialized on current policy; the emperor adopted many of his proposals.

sentences.zh: 介敢言，遇事不可，輒率同列論奏。

translations.literal: Jie dared speak; whenever something was wrong he would lead his colleagues in memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: Jie spoke boldly; whenever something was wrong he led colleagues in protest.

sentences.zh: 忤帝意，兩撻於庭。

translations.literal: He offended the emperor and was twice beaten in court.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the emperor and was beaten in court twice.

sentences.zh: 九載滿，擢大理丞，進少卿。

translations.literal: When his nine-year term expired he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and then to vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: When his nine-year term expired he rose to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then vice minister.

sentences.zh: 弘治改元，遷右僉都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: At the change to Hongzhi he was moved to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hongzhi change he became Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 尋召佐院事。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to assist at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to assist at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as Left and Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left and Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，北寇謀犯大同，命介兼左僉都御史，往督軍餉，且經略之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the tenth year northern raiders plotted to strike Datong; Jie was ordered as Left Vice Censor-in-chief to supervise military supplies and also conduct frontier policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth summer northern raiders threatened Datong; Jie was sent as Left Vice Censor-in-chief to supervise supplies and frontier policy.

sentences.zh: 比至，寇已退，乃大修戎備。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived the raiders had withdrawn, and he undertook major military preparations.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the raiders had withdrawn, and he undertook major military preparations.

sentences.zh: 察核官田牛具錢還之軍，以其資償軍所逋馬價，邊人感悅。

translations.literal: He audited official-field oxen and tool money and returned it to the troops, using the funds to cover their arrears in horse prices; border people were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He audited official-field oxen and tool funds, returned them to the troops, and used the money to cover horse-price arrears; the border people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 先後條上便宜二十事。

translations.literal: He successively memorialized twenty measures of convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized twenty practical measures in succession.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as minister.

sentences.zh: 子昆，字承裕。

translations.literal: His son Kun, styled Chengyu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kun, whose style was Chengyu.

sentences.zh: 弘治初進士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi at the opening of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 歷禮部主事。

translations.literal: He served as a clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 中官何鼎建言下獄，臺諫救之，鹹被責。

translations.literal: When the eunuch He Ding memorialized from prison, the censorate and remonstrance officials rescued him and were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuch He Ding was imprisoned for a memorial, censors and remonstrators who defended him were all punished.

sentences.zh: 昆復論救，弗聽。

translations.literal: Kun again argued for rescue but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Kun protested again but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，起改兵部主事。

translations.literal: He returned on his father mourning and on rising was changed to a clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he returned as a clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 帝將建延壽塔於城外，昆復疏諫。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to build the Longevity Pagoda outside the city; Kun again memorialized in protest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned a Longevity Pagoda outside the city; Kun protested again.

sentences.zh: 正德初，群小用事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde petty men held power.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhengde petty men held power.

sentences.zh: 請黜邪枉，進忠直，杜宦戚請乞，節中外侈費，皆不報。

translations.literal: He asked to dismiss the wicked, advance the loyal and upright, stop imperial kin from begging favors, and cut extravagant spending inside and outside the court—all without reply.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to dismiss the wicked, advance the loyal, stop imperial kin from begging favors, and cut court extravagance—all without reply.

sentences.zh: 進員外郎，忤尚書劉宇，貶知解州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director but offended Minister Liu Yu and was demoted to magistrate of Jie Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director, he offended Minister Liu Yu and was demoted to magistrate of Jie.

sentences.zh: 屢遷陜西左布政使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Shaanxi Left Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Shaanxi Left Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十年以右副都御史巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 與總督彭澤經略哈密，兵部尚書王瓊劾澤處置失宜，語連昆，下吏。

translations.literal: With Governor Peng Ze he conducted policy on Hami; Minister of War Wang Qiong impeached Ze for mishandling the affair, implicating Kun, who was sent to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: With Governor Peng Ze he handled Hami policy; Minister Wang Qiong impeached Ze and implicated Kun, who was sent to the courts.

sentences.zh: 法司言昆設謀遏強寇，功不可掩。

translations.literal: The judicial office said Kun had devised plans to check powerful bandits and his merit could not be denied.
translations.idiomatic: The courts said Kun had blocked powerful raiders and his merit could not be denied.

sentences.zh: 瓊不從，謫浙江副使。

translations.literal: Wang Qiong would not agree and demoted him to Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong refused and demoted him to Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，瓊得罪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Qiong fell from favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, Qiong fell from power.

sentences.zh: 復官，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: Kun was restored to office and grand coordinated Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was restored and grand coordinated Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 尋召為兵部右侍郎，嘉靖初，改左。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of War and in the first year of Jiajing was moved to the left.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as Right Vice Minister of War and in Jiajing's first year moved to the left.

sentences.zh: 大同軍亂，殺巡撫張文錦。

translations.literal: The Datong army mutinied and killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin.
translations.idiomatic: The Datong garrison mutinied and killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin.

sentences.zh: 昆奉命往撫，承制曲赦之，還請收恤文錦。

translations.literal: Kun was ordered to pacify them, received imperial authority to pardon them broadly, and on return asked to care for Wenjin family.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was ordered to pacify them, received authority for a broad pardon, and on return asked to aid Wenjin family.

sentences.zh: 帝方惡其激變，不從。

translations.literal: The emperor, still angry that Wenjin had provoked the mutiny, would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, still angry that Wenjin had provoked the mutiny, refused.

sentences.zh: 遇疾歸，久之卒。

translations.literal: He fell ill and returned home; after a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and went home; years later he died.

sentences.zh: 黃珂，字鳴玉，遂寧人。

translations.literal: Huang Ke, styled Mingyu, was a native of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ke, whose style was Mingyu, came from Suining.

sentences.zh: 成化二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Chenghua he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twentieth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授龍陽知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Longyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Longyang.

sentences.zh: 治行聞，擢御史，出按貴州。

translations.literal: His governance was renowned; he was promoted to investigating censor and sent to inspect Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for governance, he was promoted to investigating censor and sent to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 金達長官何輪謀不軌，計擒之，改設流官。

translations.literal: Jin Da native official He Lun plotted rebellion; Ke planned his capture and changed the post to regular administration.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Da chieftain He Lun plotted rebellion; Ke captured him and replaced native rule with regular officials.

sentences.zh: 賊婦米魯亂，奏劾巡撫錢鉞、總兵官焦俊等，皆得罪。

translations.literal: When the bandit woman Milu rebelled, he memorialized to impeach Grand Coordinator Qian Yue, Commander Jiao Jun, and others, who were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit Milu rebelled, he impeached Grand Coordinator Qian Yue and Commander Jiao Jun, who were punished.

sentences.zh: 改按畿輔，歷山西按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to inspect the capital region and served as investigating commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the capital region and served as investigating commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 正德四年，擢右僉都御史巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengde he became Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 安化王寘鐇反，傳檄四方，用討劉瑾為名。

translations.literal: The Prince of Anhua, Zhu Zhifan, rebelled and circulated proclamations everywhere, using the campaign against Liu Jin as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anhua Zhu Zhifan rebelled, circulating proclamations under the pretext of campaigning against Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 他鎮畏瑾，不敢以聞。

translations.literal: Other garrisons feared Jin and dared not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Other garrisons feared Jin and dared not report it.

sentences.zh: 珂封上其檄，因陳便宜八事，而急令副總兵侯勛、參將時源分兵扼河東，賊遂不敢出。

translations.literal: Ke sealed and forwarded the proclamation, set forth eight measures of convenience, and urgently ordered Vice Commander Hou Xun and Assistant Commander Shi Yuan to divide troops and hold the east of the river; the rebels dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Ke forwarded the proclamation, proposed eight urgent measures, and ordered Hou Xun and Shi Yuan to hold the east of the river; the rebels dared not emerge.

sentences.zh: 亦不剌寇邊，珂偕總兵官馬昂督軍戰，敗之木瓜山。

translations.literal: When Buyanara raided the border, Ke with Commander Ma Ang directed the army in battle and defeated them at Muguashan.
translations.idiomatic: When Buyanara raided the border, Ke and Commander Ma Ang defeated them at Muguashan.

sentences.zh: 六年復寇邊，珂檄副總兵王勛等七將分據要害夾擊，復敗之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year they raided again; Ke ordered Vice Commander Wang Xun and seven other generals to hold key points and strike from both sides, defeating them again.
translations.idiomatic: They raided again in the sixth year; Ke ordered Wang Xun and seven generals to hold key points and defeat them again.

sentences.zh: 屢賜璽書，銀幣。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly granted sealed edicts, silver, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly granted sealed edicts, silver, and silks.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，入為戶部右侍郎，總督倉場。

translations.literal: That autumn he entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of Revenue and supervised the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of Revenue and supervised the granaries.

sentences.zh: 河南用兵，出理軍餉。

translations.literal: When Henan was at war he went out to manage military funds.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan was at war he went out to manage military funds.

sentences.zh: 主客兵十余萬，追奔轉戰，遷止無常。

translations.literal: Host and guest armies numbered more than one hundred thousand, pursuing and fighting in constant movement with no fixed camp.
translations.idiomatic: Host and allied armies exceeded 100,000, fighting on the move with no fixed camps.

sentences.zh: 珂隨方轉輸，軍興無乏，錄功增俸一級。

translations.literal: Ke transported supplies wherever needed; the army was never short, and for merit his salary was raised one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Ke supplied them wherever they marched; the army never lacked, and his salary was raised one grade for merit.

sentences.zh: 改刑部，進左侍郎，已改佐兵部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Justice, promoted to Left Vice Minister, then changed to assist the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Justice, became Left Vice Minister, then assisted the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠謀復護衛，珂執議獨堅。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, plotted to restore his guard corps; Ke alone held firm in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao sought to restore his guard; Ke alone held firm.

sentences.zh: 九年擢南京右都御史，尋就拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Right Censor-in-chief at Nanjing and soon appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became Right Censor-in-chief at Nanjing and soon Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 以年至乞休歸，卒。

translations.literal: On grounds of age he asked to retire and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: On grounds of age he retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚簡肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Jiansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Jiansu.

sentences.zh: 王鴻儒，字懋學，南陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Hongru, styled Maoxue, was a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongru, whose style was Maoxue, came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 少工書，家貧為府書佐。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at writing; his family was poor and he served as a clerical assistant in the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he excelled at calligraphy; poor, he served as a prefectural clerk.

sentences.zh: 知府段堅愛其書，留署中，親教之。

translations.literal: Prefect Duan Jian admired his writing, kept him in the yamen, and taught him personally.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Duan Jian admired his writing, kept him in office, and taught him personally.

sentences.zh: 遣入學校為諸生，遂舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: He sent him to school as a student, and Hongru took first place in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Duan sent him to school; Hongru took first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 成化末，登進士，授南京戶部主事。

translations.literal: At the end of Chenghua he passed the jinshi and was appointed a clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Chenghua he passed the jinshi and became a clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，擢山西僉事，進副使，俱督學政。

translations.literal: He rose to director, was promoted to Shanxi Vice Commissioner, then Vice Commissioner, both times supervising education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director, became Shanxi Vice Commissioner, then Vice Commissioner, both times supervising education.

sentences.zh: 居九年，士風甚盛。

translations.literal: After nine years the scholarly ethos was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years scholarly culture flourished.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嘗語劉大夏曰：「藩臬中若王鴻儒，他日可大用也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong once said to Liu Daxia: "Among provincial officials, if there is a Wang Hongru, he may be greatly used in future.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong once told Liu Daxia, "Among provincial officials, someone like Wang Hongru may be greatly used in future.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，謝病歸。

translations.literal: When the Zhengde reign era was proclaimed, he resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengde reign, he retired on grounds of ill health.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾擅政，收召名流。

translations.literal: Liu Jin monopolized government power and summoned back renowned figures.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Jin dominating the court, distinguished officials were recalled to service.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，起為國子祭酒，以父喪去。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year he was appointed Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, but left office upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year he was recalled as Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, only to resign again when his father died.

sentences.zh: 再起南京戶部侍郎，歷吏部右侍郎，尋轉左。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Vice Minister of Revenue in Nanjing, served as Right Vice Minister of Personnel, and soon transferred to the left vice ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled once more, he became Nanjing Vice Minister of Revenue, then Right Vice Minister of Personnel, and shortly afterward moved to the left vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 十四年遷南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to be Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he rose to Nanjing Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 甫履任，宸濠反，命督軍餉，疽發於背，遂卒，謚文莊。

translations.literal: He had just taken office when the Prince of Ning, Chenghao, rebelled; he was ordered to supervise military supplies; an abscess broke out on his back, and he then died; posthumous title Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he assumed the post when the Prince of Ning rebelled and he was tasked with provisioning the army. A carbuncle erupted on his back; he died soon after and was granted the posthumous name Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 鴻儒為學，務窮理致用，為世所推。

translations.literal: Hongru in his scholarship devoted himself to thoroughly investigating principle and applying it practically, and was admired by the age.
translations.idiomatic: In his studies Hongru pursued understanding to its roots and knowledge for practical use, earning wide esteem.

sentences.zh: 左吏部，清正自持，門無私謁。

translations.literal: As Left Vice Minister of Personnel, he maintained himself with integrity and purity; no private petitions came to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Left Vice Minister of Personnel, he held himself above corruption and refused all private callers at his door.

sentences.zh: 弟鴻漸，鄉試亦第一。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hongjian also ranked first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Hongjian likewise topped the provincial exams.

sentences.zh: 以進士累官山東右布政使，以廉靜稱。

translations.literal: Through the jinshi degree he successively held office up to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong, and was known for integrity and tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi by training, he rose to Right Administration Commissioner of Shandong and was praised for upright, calm governance.

sentences.zh: 叢蘭，字廷秀，文登人。

translations.literal: Cong Lan, courtesy name Tingxiu, was a native of Wendeng.
translations.idiomatic: Cong Lan (Tingxiu), from Wendeng.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the third year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Hongzhi 3.

sentences.zh: 為戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He served as supervising secretary in the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 中官梁芳、陳喜、汪直、韋興，先以罪擯斥，復夤緣還京。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Liang Fang, Chen Xi, Wang Zhi, and Wei Xing had earlier been expelled for crimes but again, by currying favor, returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Liang Fang, Chen Xi, Wang Zhi, and Wei Xing, though previously banished for misconduct, had maneuvered their way back to court.

sentences.zh: 蘭因清寧宮災，疏陳六事，極論芳等罪，諸人遂廢。

translations.literal: Lan, on account of the fire at the Qingning Palace, memorialized setting forth six matters and strongly argued the crimes of Fang and the others; those men were thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qingning Palace burned, Cong Lan submitted a memorial outlining six reforms and fiercely denounced Fang and his associates, who were duly removed from power.

sentences.zh: 尋言：「吏部遵詔書，請擢用建言詿誤諸臣，而明旨不盡從，非所以示信。

translations.literal: Soon he said: 'The Ministry of Personnel, in accordance with an edict, requested promotion and employment of various officials who had offered advice but fallen into error; yet the clear imperial intent was not fully followed—this is not how to show good faith.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added: 'The Ministry of Personnel asked, as the edict directed, to rehabilitate ministers faulted for remonstrating—a directive the throne has only partly honored. That is a poor way to inspire trust.

sentences.zh: 失儀被糾，請免送詔獄。

translations.literal: Those subjected to discipline for breach of court ritual should be exempted from being sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Officials punished for minor breaches of ritual should not be remanded to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 畿內征徭繁重，富民規免，他戶代之，宜厘正。」

translations.literal: Within the capital region, corvée levies were heavy; wealthy households schemed to be exempted while other households were substituted in their place—this should be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée obligations in the home provinces fall hardest on the poor when the rich buy their way out and lesser households are forced to serve in their stead—that abuse must be rectified.

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was forwarded to the relevant departments.

sentences.zh: 進兵科右給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Supervising Secretary in the Department of War.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Supervising Secretary in the War Section.

sentences.zh: 都督僉事吳安以傳奉得官，蘭請罷之。

translations.literal: Assistant Regional Commander Wu An had obtained office through special appointment; Lan requested his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Wu An had been given his command through a eunuch's personal nomination; Cong Lan demanded his removal.

sentences.zh: 時命撥團營軍八千人修九門城濠，蘭言：「臣頃簡營軍，詔許專事訓練，無復差撥，命下未幾，旋復役之，如前詔何。」

translations.literal: At the time there was an order to assign eight thousand troops from the regiment camps to repair the moats of the Nine Gates. Lan said: 'Your subject recently selected camp troops; an edict permitted them to devote themselves exclusively to training, with no further reassignments. The order had scarcely been issued when they were again put to labor—what of the earlier edict?
translations.idiomatic: When eight thousand regiment troops were ordered to dig the Nine Gates moats, he protested: 'These men were just selected for training alone, by your own decree. Barely had that order been issued before they were pulled away for labor again—what value does the throne's word have?

sentences.zh: 遂罷遣。

translations.literal: They were thereupon dismissed and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: The labor draft was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 遷通政參議。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Assistant Administration Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Administration Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 小王子犯大同，命經略紫荊、倒馬諸關塞蹊隧可通敵騎者百十所。

translations.literal: When the Little Prince invaded Datong, he was ordered to oversee defense of over a hundred paths and tunnels in passes such as Zijing and Daoma through which enemy cavalry could pass.
translations.idiomatic: During the Little Prince's attack on Datong, he was charged with fortifying more than a hundred mountain defiles at Zijing, Daoma, and other passes where enemy horsemen might break through.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進左通政。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde he was promoted to Left Administration Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 3 he advanced to Left Administration Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年冬出理延綏屯田。

translations.literal: The next year, winter, he went out to administer military colonies in Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was sent to manage frontier garrison farms in Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 安化王寘鐇反，蘭奏陳十事，中言：「文武官罰米者，鬻產不能償。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Anhua, Zhu Zhifan, rebelled, Lan memorialized setting forth ten matters, among which he said: 'Civil and military officials subjected to grain fines sell their property yet still cannot repay.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Anhua rebelled, Cong Lan submitted a ten-point memorial, noting among other things: 'Officials fined in grain must sell their estates and still cannot make payment.

sentences.zh: 朝臣謫戍，刑官妄引新例鍛煉成獄，沒其家貲。

translations.literal: Court ministers banished to frontier garrison—judicial officials rashly cite new precedents and forge cases, confiscating their family property.
translations.idiomatic: Banished courtiers are framed under novel legal pretexts and stripped of their estates.

sentences.zh: 校尉遍行邊塞，勢焰薰灼，人不自保。」

translations.literal: Commandants of the Embroidered Uniform Guard run rampant through border regions; their power scorches all around, and people cannot protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Embroidered Uniform Guard runners prowl the borderlands, their arrogance unbearable—no one dares feel safe.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾大惡之，矯旨嚴責。

translations.literal: Liu Jin greatly hated this; he forged an edict and severely rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin was furious and issued a forged imperial reprimand.

sentences.zh: 給事中張瓚、御史汪賜等遂希旨劾蘭。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Zhang Zan and censor Wang Ci and others thereupon, seeking to please, impeached Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zan, Wang Ci, and other officials dutifully impeached Cong Lan at Liu Jin's cue.

sentences.zh: 瑾方憂邊事，置不問。

translations.literal: Jin was just then concerned with border affairs and set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Preoccupied with border crises, Liu Jin let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 數月，瑾誅，進通政使。

translations.literal: Several months later, Jin was executed; Lan was promoted to Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Months later, after Liu Jin's fall, Cong Lan was promoted to Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俄擢戶部右侍郎，督理三邊軍餉。

translations.literal: Soon he was elevated to Right Vice Minister of Revenue and supervised provision of military supplies for the Three Frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Right Vice Minister of Revenue, overseeing provisioning for the northwestern frontier.

sentences.zh: 六年，陜西巡撫都御史藍章以四月寇亂移駐漢中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Lan Zhang, Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi, relocated his headquarters to Hanzhong in the fourth month due to bandit disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, after April raiding forced Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Lan Zhang to shift his base to Hanzhong,

sentences.zh: 會河套有警，乃命蘭兼管固、靖等處軍務。

translations.literal: Just then there was an alarm from the Ordos region; Lan was therefore ordered concurrently to manage military affairs in Gu and Jing and other places.
translations.idiomatic: An alarm from the Ordos loop then led to his concurrent appointment over military affairs at Guzhou, Jingzhou, and adjacent districts.

sentences.zh: 蘭上言：「陜西起運糧草，數為大戶侵牟，請委官押送。

translations.literal: Lan memorialized: 'In Shaanxi, transport of grain and fodder is repeatedly exploited by powerful households; please assign officials to escort deliveries.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that Shaanxi's grain and fodder convoys, long prey to local magnates, be placed under official escort.

sentences.zh: 每鎮請發內帑銀數萬，預賣糧草。

translations.literal: For each garrison he requested disbursement of tens of thousands of taels from the inner treasury to sell grain and fodder in advance.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed advanced grain sales at each garrison, funded by tens of thousands of taels from the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 御史張彧清出田畝，請蠲免子粒，如弘治十八年以前科則。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Yu had cleared and registered field acreage; he requested exemption from grain tax according to the tax rates before the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Following Censor Zhang Yu's land survey, he asked that grain levies revert to pre-Hongzhi-18 rates.

sentences.zh: 靈州鹽課，請照例開中，召商糴糧。

translations.literal: Regarding Lingzhou salt revenue, he requested opening salt license sales according to precedent to summon merchants to purchase grain.
translations.idiomatic: For Lingzhou salt revenues, he recommended reviving the salt certificate system to attract merchants to supply grain.

sentences.zh: 軍士折色，主者多克減，乞選委鄰近有司散給。」

translations.literal: When soldiers received cash commutation, those in charge often cut and reduced payments; he begged that nearby local officials be selected and delegated to distribute payments.
translations.idiomatic: Cash stipends for troops were routinely skimmed by paymasters; he asked that nearby civil officials distribute them instead.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His requests were granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，南畿及河南歲侵，命蘭往振。

translations.literal: That year, winter, the Southern Capital region and Henan suffered annual crop failure; Lan was ordered to go provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, famine struck the southern capital provinces and Henan, and Cong Lan was dispatched to administer relief.

sentences.zh: 未赴而河北賊自宿遷渡河，將逼鳳陽。

translations.literal: Before he could go, bandits in Hebei crossed the river from Suqian and were about to threaten Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, Hebei rebels crossed the Huai from Suqian and threatened Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 乃命蘭以本官巡視廬、鳳、滁、和，兼理振濟。

translations.literal: Lan was therefore ordered, in his existing office, to inspect Lu, Feng, Chu, and He, and concurrently administer relief.
translations.idiomatic: He was redirected to inspect Luzhou, Fengyang, Chuzhou, and Hezhou while continuing famine relief.

sentences.zh: 河南白蓮賊趙景隆自稱宋王，掠歸德，蘭遣指揮石堅、知州張思齊等擊斬之。

translations.literal: The Henan White Lotus bandit Zhao Jinglong proclaimed himself King of Song and plundered Guide; Lan sent Commander Shi Jian, Prefect Zhang Siqi, and others to attack and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Henan White Lotus rebel Zhao Jinglong styled himself King of Song and raided Guide, Cong Lan sent Commander Shi Jian and Prefect Zhang Siqi to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 九月，賊平。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month the rebellion was suppressed.

sentences.zh: 論功賚金幣，增俸一級，召還理部事。

translations.literal: For merits he was rewarded with gold and silks, given one rank increase in salary, and recalled to manage ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received gold and silk, a pay grade, and recall to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 部無侍郎缺，乃命添註。

translations.literal: There was no vice-minister vacancy in the ministry, so he was ordered added as a supernumerary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: With no regular vice-ministership open, he was given a supernumerary slot.

sentences.zh: 明年，大同有警，命巡視居庸、龍泉諸關。

translations.literal: The next year, with alarm at Datong, he was ordered to inspect the passes at Juyong, Longquan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, amid Datong alarms, he was sent to inspect Juyong, Longquan, and other passes.

sentences.zh: 尋兼督宣、大軍餉，進右都御史，總制宣、大、山東軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was also charged with supervising military supplies for Xuan and Da, promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief, and given overall command of military affairs in Xuan, Da, and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of Xuanfu-Datong provisioning, rose to Right Censor-in-Chief, and assumed overall military command in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 令內地皆築堡，寇至收保如塞下。

translations.literal: He ordered that throughout the interior fortresses be built; when bandits arrived, people would take refuge in them as on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He had fortresses built across the interior so that, when raiders came, the populace could shelter as they did on the border.

sentences.zh: 寇五萬騎自萬全右衛趨蔚州大掠，又三萬騎入平虜南城，以失事停半歲俸。

translations.literal: Bandits with fifty thousand horsemen from Wanquan Right Guard rushed toward Yuzhou and looted extensively; another thirty thousand horsemen entered Pinglu South City; for the failure he was suspended from half a year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand horsemen from Wanquan Right Guard swept through Yuzhou; thirty thousand more broke into Pinglu's south fort—Cong Lan lost six months' pay for the lapse.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，改督漕運，尋兼巡撫江北。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, summer, he was changed to supervise grain transport, and soon also served concurrently as Grand Coordinator of Jiangbei.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth summer he was transferred to supervise the Grand Canal, then also made Grand Coordinator of Jiangbei.

sentences.zh: 中官劉允取佛烏思藏，道蘭境，入謁，辭不見。

translations.literal: The eunuch Liu Yun, traveling to retrieve Buddhist texts from the Western Regions, passed through Lan's jurisdiction; he came to pay his respects, but Lan declined to see him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liu Yun, en route to fetch Buddhist texts from the West, passed through his territory and sought an audience; Cong Lan refused.

sentences.zh: 允需舟五百余艘、役夫萬余人，蘭馳疏極陳其害。

translations.literal: Yun required more than five hundred boats and over ten thousand corvée laborers; Lan urgently memorialized, strongly setting forth the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun demanded five hundred boats and ten thousand laborers; Cong Lan rushed a memorial detailing the damage this would cause.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored him.

sentences.zh: 居四年，以事忤兵部尚書王瓊，解漕務，專任巡撫。

translations.literal: After four years, over a matter he offended Minister of War Wang Qiong, was relieved of grain transport duties, and served exclusively as Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he clashed with War Minister Wang Qiong, lost the canal post, and served solely as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠反，蘭移鎮瓜州。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning, Chenghao, rebelled, Lan shifted his headquarters to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ning rebelled, he moved his command to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Minister of Works in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became Nanjing Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 吳世忠，字懋貞，金溪人。

translations.literal: Wu Shizhong, courtesy name Maozhen, was a native of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shizhong (Maozhen), from Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the third year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Hongzhi 3.

sentences.zh: 授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Department of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a War Section supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 兩畿及山東、河南、浙江民饑，有詔振恤，所司俟勘覆。

translations.literal: The Two Capital regions and Shandong, Henan, and Zhejiang suffered famine among the people; there was an edict for relief, but responsible offices awaited investigation and review.
translations.idiomatic: Famine afflicted the capital provinces, Shandong, Henan, and Zhejiang; though relief was ordered, local offices dragged their feet pending verification.

sentences.zh: 世忠極言其弊，因條上興水利、復常平二事，多施行。

translations.literal: Shizhong strongly set forth these abuses and, in itemized form, submitted two matters—reviving water conservancy and restoring ever-normal granaries—many of which were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shizhong exposed the delay and proposed restoring waterworks and ever-normal granaries—most of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 已，請恤建文朝殉難諸臣，乞賜爵謚，崇廟食，且錄其子孫，復其族屬，為忠義勸。

translations.literal: Thereafter he requested favor for various officials who suffered martyrdom in the Jianwen reign, begging enfeoffment, posthumous titles, elevation with temple sacrifices, and moreover recording their descendants and restoring their clansmen, to encourage loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned honors for Jianwen-era martyrs—titles, posthumous names, temple sacrifices, rehabilitation of their heirs—in the hope of inspiring future loyalty.

sentences.zh: 章下禮官，寢不行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the Ministry of Rites; it was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites Ministry received the proposal and quietly shelved it.

sentences.zh: 尚書王恕被訐求去，上疏請留之。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Shu was impeached and sought to leave; he memorialized requesting his retention.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Wang Shu was attacked and sought to resign, Wu Shizhong memorialized asking the emperor to keep him.

sentences.zh: 壽寧侯張鶴齡求勘河間賜地，其母金夫人復求不已。

translations.literal: Marquis of Shouning Zhang Heling sought surveying of granted land in Hejian; his mother Lady Jin repeatedly pressed her demands without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Shouning, Zhang Heling, wanted a survey of his Hejian estate; his mother, Lady Jin, kept pressing the claim.

sentences.zh: 帝命遣使，世忠言：「侯家仰托肺腑，豈宜與小民爭尺寸？

translations.literal: The emperor ordered envoys dispatched; Shizhong said: 'The marquis's household enjoys the emperor's closest trust—how should they wrangle with common people over inches?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sent surveyors, Wu Shizhong argued: 'A household so close to the throne should not haggle with commoners over scraps of land.

sentences.zh: 命部勘未已，內臣繼之。

translations.literal: The order for the ministry to survey had not yet ended when inner court eunuchs followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner had one ministry survey begun than palace eunuchs launched another.

sentences.zh: 內臣未已，大臣又繼之。

translations.literal: Before the eunuchs had finished, grand ministers followed again in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before the eunuchs finished, senior ministers were dispatched anew.

sentences.zh: 剝民斂怨，非國家福，龍非外戚之福。」

translations.literal: Exploiting the people and gathering resentment is no blessing to the state, nor to the imperial in-laws.
translations.idiomatic: Such exactions breed public anger—bad for the realm and worse for the imperial in-laws themselves.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 大同總兵官神英、副總兵趙昶等，因馬市令家人以違禁彩繒易馬，番人因闌入私易鐵器。

translations.literal: Datong Commander-in-Chief Shen Ying, Deputy Commander Zhao Chang, and others, on account of the horse market, had household members exchange horses for forbidden colored silks; the tribesmen took advantage to smuggle in and privately exchange iron implements.
translations.idiomatic: At Datong, Commander Shen Ying and Deputy Zhao Chang allowed their households to trade banned silks at the horse market; tribesmen slipped through to trade ironware on the side.

sentences.zh: 既出塞，復潛兵掠蔚州，陷馬營，轉剽中東二路。

translations.literal: After leaving the frontier, they again secretly sent troops to raid Yuzhou, capture Macheng, and turn to plunder the Central and Eastern Routes.
translations.idiomatic: Once beyond the passes they secretly raided Yuzhou, seized Macheng, and ravaged the Central and Eastern routes.

sentences.zh: 英等擁兵不救，巡撫劉瓛、鎮守中官孫振又不以實聞。

translations.literal: Ying and others held troops but did not rescue; Grand Coordinator Liu Fan and the garrison eunuch Sun Zhen also did not report the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ying kept his troops idle; Grand Coordinator Liu Fan and garrison eunuch Sun Zhen covered up the facts.

sentences.zh: 十一年，事發，世忠往勘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the affair came to light; Shizhong went to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When the scandal broke in the eleventh year, Wu Shizhong was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 上疏備陳大同邊備廢馳、士卒困苦之狀。

translations.literal: He memorialized fully setting forth the state of Datong frontier defense in neglect and soldiers in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial detailed Datong's collapsed defenses and the troops' misery.

sentences.zh: 因極言英、瓛等貪利畏敵，蕩無法度。

translations.literal: He thereby strongly stated that Ying, Fan, and others were greedy for profit, feared the enemy, and utterly lacked discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced Shen Ying, Liu Fan, and their ilk for greed, cowardice, and total indiscipline.

sentences.zh: 英落職，瓛、振召還，昶及遊擊劉淮、參將李嶼等俱逮問。

translations.literal: Ying was stripped of office; Fan and Zhen were recalled; Chang and Mobile Corps Commander Liu Huai, Assistant Commander Li Yu, and others were all arrested for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ying was dismissed; Liu Fan and Sun Zhen recalled; Zhao Chang, Liu Huai, Li Yu, and others arrested.

sentences.zh: 已而瓛改大理少卿，昶以大理丞吳一貫覆訁獻僅鐫級。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fan was transferred to Vice Minister of the Dali Court; Chang, upon re-examination by Dali Court Vice Minister Wu Yiguan, was merely demoted one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan was reassigned to the Dali Court while Zhao Chang, on review by Wu Yiguan, escaped with a single rank demotion.

sentences.zh: 世忠復極論瓛罪，且詆一貫，帝皆不問。

translations.literal: Shizhong again strongly argued Fan's crimes and also slandered Wu Yiguan; the emperor paid no attention to any of it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shizhong renewed his attack on Liu Fan and denounced Wu Yiguan; the emperor ignored him.

sentences.zh: 闕里文廟災，陳八事，不能盡用。

translations.literal: When the Confucian temple at Qufu burned, he set forth eight matters; they could not all be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qufu Confucian temple burned, his eight-point program was only partly adopted.

sentences.zh: 寇犯延綏、大同，世忠言：「國初設七十二衛，軍士不下百萬。

translations.literal: When bandits invaded Yan-sui and Datong, Shizhong said: 'At the founding of the state, seventy-two guards were established and soldiers numbered no less than a million.
translations.idiomatic: During raids on Yan-sui and Datong, he warned: 'At the dynasty's founding, seventy-two guards fielded over a million men.

sentences.zh: 近軍政日壞，精卒不能得一二萬人。

translations.literal: Recently military administration daily deteriorates; elite troops cannot amount to even ten or twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Today the army rots until barely ten or twenty thousand effective soldiers remain.

sentences.zh: 此兵足憂也。

translations.literal: This matter of troops is sufficient cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Our military strength should alarm us.

sentences.zh: 太倉之儲，本以備軍。

translations.literal: The granary stores at Taicang were originally to prepare for the army.
translations.idiomatic: Taicang's granaries were meant to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 近支費日廣，移用日多。

translations.literal: Recently expenditures daily expand and diversions for other uses daily increase.
translations.idiomatic: Lately spending grows and funds are diverted elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 倘興師十萬，犒賜無所取給。

translations.literal: If we were to raise an army of one hundred thousand, there would be nowhere from which to obtain rewards and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Raise a hundred-thousand-man army today and there is nothing left for rations or bonuses.

sentences.zh: 此食足憂也。

translations.literal: This matter of provisions is sufficient cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Our logistics should alarm us.

sentences.zh: 正統己巳之變尚有石亨、楊洪，邇所用李杲、阮興、趙昶、劉淮之屬，先後皆敗。

translations.literal: At the Jisi crisis of Zhengtong there were still Shi Heng and Yang Hong; those recently employed, men like Li Gao, Ruan Xing, Zhao Chang, and Liu Huai, have one after another all been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Jisi crisis still had Shi Heng and Yang Hong; recent appointees like Li Gao, Ruan Xing, Zhao Chang, and Liu Huai have all failed in turn.

sentences.zh: 今王璽、馬昇又以失事告。

translations.literal: Now Wang Xi and Ma Sheng have again been reported for failure in duty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi and Ma Sheng have just been censured for bungling their commands.

sentences.zh: 此將帥足憂也。

translations.literal: This matter of generals and commanders is sufficient cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Our commanders should alarm us.

sentences.zh: 國家多事，大臣有以鎮之。

translations.literal: When the state faces many affairs, grand ministers are what stabilize it.
translations.idiomatic: In troubled times, great ministers hold the state steady.

sentences.zh: 邇者忠正多斥，貪庸獲存。

translations.literal: Recently the loyal and upright are largely expelled; the greedy and mediocre survive.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the honest are purged while the mediocre and corrupt remain.

sentences.zh: 既鮮匡濟之才，又昧去就之節，安能懾強敵壯國勢乎？

translations.literal: Since there is scarce talent to aid and rescue, and they are ignorant of the integrity of advancing or withdrawing—how can they awe strong enemies and strengthen the nation's momentum?
translations.idiomatic: With few capable statesmen and no sense of honor, how can we deter powerful foes or strengthen the realm?

sentences.zh: 此任人足憂也。

translations.literal: This matter of employing men is sufficient cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Our choice of men should alarm us.

sentences.zh: 政多舛乖，民日咨怨。

translations.literal: Government has many errors and contradictions; the people daily groan with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Policy blunders multiply and popular resentment grows daily.

sentences.zh: 京軍敝力役，京民苦催科，畿甸覬恩尤切。

translations.literal: Capital troops are worn down by corvée labor; capital people suffer under tax collection; those in the capital region especially long for grace.
translations.idiomatic: Capital garrisons are exhausted by labor levies, city dwellers crushed by taxes—the home provinces desperately need relief.

sentences.zh: 顧使不樂其生至此，臨難誰與死守？

translations.literal: Yet if people are made so unhappy with their lives as this, when facing difficulty who will join in a death grip defense with them?
translations.idiomatic: When life has become this bitter, who will stand and die defending the realm?

sentences.zh: 此民心足憂也。

translations.literal: This matter of popular sentiment is sufficient cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Public morale should alarm us.

sentences.zh: 天變屢征，火患頻發。

translations.literal: Heavenly anomalies repeatedly appear as portents; fire disasters frequently break out.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends repeated omens; fires break out again and again.

sentences.zh: 雲南地震壓萬余家，大同馬災踣二千匹。

translations.literal: An earthquake in Yunnan crushed over ten thousand households; a horse disaster at Datong caused two thousand horses to collapse.
translations.idiomatic: An earthquake in Yunnan destroyed ten thousand homes; two thousand horses perished at Datong.

sentences.zh: 此天意足憂也。

translations.literal: This matter of Heaven's intent is sufficient cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's displeasure should alarm us.

sentences.zh: 願順好惡以收人心，肅念慮以回天意，遣文武重臣經略宣、大，以飭邊防。

translations.literal: I wish that you accord with likes and dislikes to win back popular hearts, solemnize thought and consideration to turn back Heaven's intent, and dispatch important civil and military ministers to manage Xuan and Da and rectify border defense.
translations.idiomatic: Align your preferences with the people's, govern with sober purpose to appease Heaven, and send senior civil and military officers to secure Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 策免諸臣不肖者，而起素有才望，如何喬新、劉大夏、倪嶽、戴珊、張敷華、林俊諸人，以任國事。

translations.literal: Remove unworthy ministers and raise men of long-standing talent and reputation, such as Qiao Xin, Liu Daxia, Ni Yue, Dai Shan, Zhang Fuhua, and Lin Jun, to entrust with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dismiss the unfit and recall proven statesmen—Qiao Xin, Liu Daxia, Ni Yue, Dai Shan, Zhang Fuhua, Lin Jun—to manage affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 則賊將望風遠循，而邊境可無憂矣。」

translations.literal: Then bandits will flee at the mere sight of the wind from afar, and the borderlands can be free of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies would flee at a rumor, and the frontier would be secure.

sentences.zh: 帝以言多詆毀，切責之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the words contained much slander, sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, offended by the imputations, rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 尋乞大同增置臺堡，以閑田給軍耕墾，不征其稅。

translations.literal: Soon he requested added watch-towers and fortresses at Datong, granting idle fields to soldiers for farming and reclamation, without levying tax on them.
translations.idiomatic: He later proposed new watchtowers at Datong, assigning fallow land to garrison farmers tax-free.

sentences.zh: 江西歲饑盜起，請簡巡撫，黜有司貪殘者。

translations.literal: Jiangxi suffered yearly famine and banditry arose; he requested selection of a grand coordinator and dismissal of greedy and cruel local officials.
translations.idiomatic: When famine and banditry struck Jiangxi, he urged appointing a strong grand coordinator and removing corrupt local officials.

sentences.zh: 又請築京師外城。

translations.literal: He also requested construction of the outer wall of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also called for building Beijing's outer city walls.

sentences.zh: 所司多從其議。

translations.literal: Responsible offices largely followed his recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏科左給事中，擢湖廣參議，坐事降山東僉事。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Left Supervising Secretary in the Department of Personnel, elevated to Assistant Administration Commissioner of Huguang, then demoted to Vice Commissioner of Shandong for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After further promotion in the Personnel Section and appointment as Huguang Assistant Commissioner, an offense reduced him to Shandong Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 正德四年閏九月召為光祿少卿，旋改尚寶司卿。

translations.literal: In the intercalary ninth month of the fourth year of Zhengde he was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment, and soon changed to Director of the Directorate of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled in the intercalary ninth month of Zhengde 4 as Vice Director of Imperial Banquets, he was soon made Director of the Directorate of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，與通政叢蘭等出理邊屯，世忠往薊州。

translations.literal: That year, winter, together with Administration Commissioner Cong Lan and others he went out to administer frontier colonies; Shizhong went to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he joined Cong Lan and others inspecting frontier garrison farms, with Wu Shizhong assigned to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年奏言：「占種盜賣，積弊已久。

translations.literal: The next year he memorialized: 'Illegal occupation and cultivation and theft in selling—accumulated abuses have long existed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he reported: 'Illegal planting and illicit sales are chronic abuses.

sentences.zh: 若一一究問，恐人情不安，請量為處分。」

translations.literal: If each case is investigated one by one, I fear popular sentiment will be unsettled; I request measured disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Prosecuting every case would unsettle the region—he asked for tempered penalties.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾敗，言官劾其嘗請清核屯田，助瑾為虐。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin fell, censorial officials impeached him for having once requested thorough verification of garrison farms, aiding Jin in tyranny.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin's fall, censors accused him of aiding the eunuch by ordering a harsh audit of garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 世忠故方鯁，朝議寬之，得免。

translations.literal: Shizhong had always been upright and unyielding; court opinion was lenient toward him, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Known for stubborn integrity, he was spared by prevailing court sympathy.

sentences.zh: 再遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Minister of the Dali Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Vice Minister of the Dali Court.

sentences.zh: 八年擢右僉都御史巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was elevated to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 寇在河套，逐之失利，乃引疾歸。

translations.literal: Bandits were in the Ordos; pursuit met with failure; he therefore cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After failing to drive Ordos raiders back, he retired claiming illness.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明至英宗以後，幸門日開。

translations.literal: The commentator says: From the time of the Ming reaching Yingzong and afterward, the gate of favor daily opened wider.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: After Emperor Yingzong, the door to imperial favor swung ever wider.

sentences.zh: 傳奉請乞，官冗役繁，用度奓汰，盛極孽衰，國計坐絀。

translations.literal: Special appointments and petitions, redundant offices and heavy corvée, expenditures extravagantly inflated—when flourishing reached its peak, calamity followed decline; the national accounts sat in deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch appointments, bloated bureaucracy, crushing levies, and runaway spending marked the turn from apex to ruin—state finances sank into chronic deficit.

sentences.zh: 李敏諸人斤斤為國惜財，抵抗近幸，以求紓民。

translations.literal: Li Min and others painstakingly economized on behalf of the state, resisted close favorites, seeking to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Li Min scrimped for the treasury, resisted the emperor's intimates, and tried to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 然涓滴之助，無補漏卮。

translations.literal: Yet help in drops and trickles could not repair a leaking vessel.
translations.idiomatic: But pennies saved could not stop a sinking ship.

sentences.zh: 國家當承平殷阜之世，侈心易萌。

translations.literal: The state, while in an era of peace and abundance, easily nurtures extravagance of heart.
translations.idiomatic: In times of peace and plenty, extravagance takes root easily.

sentences.zh: 近習乘之，糜費日廣。

translations.literal: Close associates take advantage of this; wasteful spending daily expands.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favorites exploited that weakness, and waste grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「節以制度，不傷財，不害民」，又曰「不節若，則嗟若」，此恭儉之主所為凜凜也。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Regulate through institutions—do not harm wealth, do not injure the people"; it also says "If there is no regulation, then comes lamentation"—this is why reverent and frugal rulers act with such awe.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes warns: "Regulate through institutions—do not harm wealth or injure the people"; and "Without restraint comes lamentation"—hence the vigilance of truly frugal rulers.
